name: CommandPalette
description: Cmd/Ctrl+K command palette: board-wide commands plus actions for the card that held keyboard focus when the palette opened (issue #101, Direction B).
usage: Mounted once in pages/tasks.vue; open with Cmd/Ctrl+K. Desktop/keyboard only (no entry point on mobile).
avoid: Not for pointer navigation (AppNav, MorePanel); desktop and keyboard only, there is no entry point on a phone.
responsibility: Render UCommandPalette inside UModal; Esc closes and focus returns to the card
Show the shortcut hints of the commands (`kbds`) and the palette's own keys in the footer
Empty and loading states; screen-reader result status via role="status"

name: AddTaskSlot
description: Card-sized add control that morphs into the draft card of the task being added, in the same box (#125). Its soft surface rests label-wide and grows into the card shape on hover/focus (#466)
usage: Offen: last item of the task list (BoardColumn). Jetzt: overlay of the empty column (BoardColumnProgressContent), opens add-and-start
avoid: Not the full add form: the sheet's TaskForm adds with all fields, NewCardFlow asks the guided questions; not for editing an existing task.
responsibility: Native button named by its visible label, in a regular card's box (width, --task-card-height, card radius); the box never changes size, so layout, hit area and DnD rects stay put

Inside the button, `.add-task-button-surface` (centred icon + label on --ui-bg-muted, button radius) is the visible shape. Offen: label-wide at rest (2.25rem = 36px on desktop, the height of the day-close `lg` button beside it, #582; 3rem on mobile, where `lg` is 48px), grows to the card box over --add-slot-grow-duration on hover (pointer devices only, so a tap never sticks), focus-visible and while drafting (held grown, so it does not jump back under the fading label); the label stays centred throughout. Growth animates min-width/min-height inside the fixed box (an accepted trade-off: a transform would distort radius and label)
Offen on mobile: a sticky 48px bar (#33) that swaps for the draft at the end of the list (#110); the surface never grows there

Jetzt: the `icon` prop (lightning) and the label say it starts a task now; the surface is always the full card shape; on pointer devices surface and label appear only while the Jetzt section is hovered or the slot has focus; touch shows the label at rest
While the in-card form is open the Jetzt focus overlay steps aside (useInCardAdding, kd#56)
Drafting (useTaskDraft holds a draft for this column): the draft card fades in over the button, the label fades out; the button stays mounted but inert, so focus can return to it

In-card adding (#649, `inCard`, Offen): the button opens NewCardFlow in the same box instead of the sheet and the slot is held grown like for a draft. Esc on a typed title also shows a "Rückgängig" toast that reopens the card with it (#665). Esc, a press outside a blank card, the sheet opening or a drag cancel it and send focus back to the button; a save swaps it for the saved card (no fade) and focuses that card. Jetzt and every other entry (palette, nav, menu) keep the sheet

The slot is a raw `<button>` on purpose (#71, audit): a card-shaped target whose box is reserved and held while a draft or a drag runs (`add-task-button`, `data-add-slot`, `inert`), which `UButton ghost block` cannot reproduce; revisit with the redesign (#1)
During a drag (`hidden`) the slot keeps its geometry but is invisible and not interactive
Reserves the card box only for the button or the draft: with neither (`showButton` off, no draft) it takes no space

name: Board
description: Main kanban board component that organizes and displays tasks by status
usage: Used on the main page to provide the core task management interface
avoid: Not for one column or one card (BoardColumn, TaskCard); mounted once per page, never nested.
responsibility: Renders the complete kanban board with all columns
Manages drag-and-drop functionality between columns
Handles task status changes and column order updates
Provides visual feedback during task interactions

Phone: three column pages moved by swipe and drag edge-scroll only (no tabs, #470); the active page is `data-mobile-page` and focus entering an off-screen page makes it active (the keyboard / screen-reader path the tabs were)
Phone: BoardPageDots, a non-interactive three-dot page indicator above the column title (kd#26)
Erledigt footer: the "Tag abschließen" CTA while something is done today

name: BoardColumn
description: Column component for the kanban board that displays tasks of a specific status
usage: Used within the main board layout to organize tasks by their status
avoid: Not for the Jetzt column, whose single card has its own content (BoardColumnProgressContent); not a drop target on its own (ColumnDropZone).
responsibility: Displays tasks of a specific status (Today, Doing, Waiting, Done)

Grouped columns: renders each group of 2+ as a collapsed TaskStack or, once expanded, as a header row (#148) and ordinary sortable cards (#147); owns the outside-click/Escape/"Schließen" collapse of its stacks
Renders dedicated progress bar section for Progress column (separate from task list)
Provides header with status information
Enables task addition for the Open column (card-sized add slot that morphs into the draft, #125)
Handles visual states for different statuses and empty states
Erledigt drop target (#124): a light teal wash under the list and a one-line hint while a card from another column hovers it

name: BoardColumnHeader
description: Header component for kanban board columns
usage: Used at the top of each BoardColumn to display status title and visual indicators
avoid: Not a page header (PageHeader) and not the header of an expanded stack (TaskStackHeader).
responsibility: Displays column title with appropriate styling
Shows status-specific icons (checkmark for Done column)
Handles visual states for different statuses (waiting, empty)

name: BoardColumnItem
description: One element of a standard column's task list: a collapsed stack, the header row of an expanded one, or a sortable card
usage: Rendered by BoardColumn, one per list item
avoid: Not for the Jetzt column (BoardColumnProgressContent) and not for a card outside a column list; use TaskCard directly for a static card.
responsibility: Renders the slot of a card deleted inside its undo window as TaskDeletedGap (#422): not a sortable, no drag, no drop

Renders a collapsed group as TaskStack (one sortable by its front task, #150), the header row of an expanded one as TaskStackHeader (not a sortable: it sits next to the sortables, never inside one), anything else as SortableTaskWrapper > context menu > TaskCard (the same markup for an ungrouped card, a single-card group and a member of an expanded stack)

Has exactly one root element per item (no fragment). dnd-kit moves the dragged wrapper next to its target and Vue removes a fragment by walking its anchors: a card that sat in another card's fragment would be removed with it (#146). One root node per item keeps the list flat.

name: BoardColumnProgressContent
description: Specialized content for the Progress column
usage: Rendered by BoardColumn for the Jetzt column only
avoid: Only for the Jetzt column; the other columns render lists through BoardColumnItem.
responsibility: Renders the task list for "In Progress" tasks
Displays the dedicated progress bar for the active task
Hosts the add-and-start slot while Jetzt is empty (#125); it morphs into the Jetzt draft card
Manages specific layout requirements for the progress column

name: BoardColumnYesterdayNote
description: One-line "Gestern erledigt" note on a soft Done-Teal surface at the top of the Done column
usage: Rendered by BoardColumn above today's done list while tasks finished before today are not acknowledged
avoid: Only above the Erledigt list; not for an alert or an error (use a UAlert or the sync popover).
responsibility: Show an honest day label (yesterday / weekday / recently) and the count on one line; the label button opens the titles in place (aria-expanded, local view state, never persisted)
Opened: at most five titles as quiet rows (time spent on the right, hidden at zero) that open the task sheet, then "+ n weitere"
Offer exactly one action ("Gesehen") on the line; the parent archives all tasks of the note
Keep today's wins on top: `--task-note-height` collapsed, 42px on desktop (46px at 390px so both controls reach 44px), card width, centred

Surface (#605, D2; outline dropped #57): no border, `--done-note-wash` (70 % `success-100` over `success-50`: darker than the in-card confirmation wash so it separates without a frame, short of the `success-100` Erledigt drop wash so it never reads as a drop target), card radius. Tick and "Gesehen" in `success-800`; title row neutral, rows `toned`

Its three controls (label toggle, "Gesehen", title rows) are `UButton` ghost neutral (#71): the theme brings focus ring, hover wash and the 44 px phone floor; the note's scoped CSS keeps only its geometry, type and colours. The toggle stays a button inside the `<h3>` (`aria-expanded`)
Collapse over 180ms when it leaves (instant under prefers-reduced-motion); the caret rotates 180ms

name: BoardPageDots
description: Phone page indicator: three dots above the column title, the active one a stretched pill
usage: Rendered once by Board.vue beside .board (so it does not slide with the pages)
avoid: Phone only, for the three board pages; not a tab bar or pagination on desktop.
responsibility: Says that three pages exist (Offen, Jetzt + Wartet, Erledigt) and which one is showing (kd#26)
Follows a live swipe: the pill stretches from one dot to the next with the finger, then settles on the board's own timing

Pure indicator: not focusable, not tappable (`pointer-events: none`, `aria-hidden`), so it is no tab bar (#470, ADR 017); the page is already exposed by the column headings and `data-mobile-page`, a hidden "page 2 of 3" would say it twice

Phone only (display none from 768 px; scoped CSS, since an unlayered `display: flex` beats the layered `md:hidden`); `prefers-reduced-motion` drops the settle transition Accepted trade-off: dots 6 px (`--page-dot`), active pill 20 px; colours `--ui-border-accented` and `--ui-text-muted`, no text.

name: ColumnDropZone
description: Invisible droppable sentinel for each board column. Ensures @dnd-kit/vue can accept drops even when a column has no sortable items. Uses useDroppable with data.taskStatus so useBoardDndKit.onDragEnd can identify the target column for cross-column transfers. Ghost placeholder visibility: - Empty columns: isDropTarget becomes true when ColumnDropZone wins collision (collisionPriority: 0 guarantees sortables always win on non-empty columns) - Non-empty columns: dnd-kit's sortable handles insertion preview via .kando-dnd-dragged moving physically to the destination — no ghost needed here - A column whose only card (or stack) is the one being dragged counts as empty once dnd-kit moved that node into another column (#372): it is judged by its list's DOM, not by the store, which still holds the task. The ghost shows there; the node stays in the other column, its slot made transparent by the same `:has(.column-drop-zone__ghost)` rule as for any empty target (taken out of the layout when other cards remain there, so they leave no gap, #393). The DOM answer is re-read whenever the list's children change during a drag (dnd-kit moves the node after the zone became the target) - A refused drop (the WIP limit, or any stack into Jetzt, #150) shows no ghost: the slot would promise a landing
usage: Rendered once per BoardColumn so an empty column still accepts a drop
avoid: Invisible; never a visible drop target and never outside a board column (the sortable cards are the visible targets).

name: ColumnSortingControl
description: Per-column sort menu in the column header: sort field and direction for one column
usage: Rendered by BoardColumn; fades out while not hovered or focused (`visible`)
avoid: Sorts one column only; board-wide controls (grouping, day close) live in MorePanel.
responsibility: List the sort options for the column's status, mark the active one
Emit `change` (field, direction) and `open-change` so the header can keep the control visible while the menu is open

name: DayCloseBody
description: Scrolling content of the closing step (#98): what got done today, what is not done yet, one closing line.
usage: Hosted by DayCloseDialog (modal and drawer share it). Reads the local cache only; a sync that lands while it is open updates the lists in place.
avoid: Not standalone: hosted by DayCloseDialog (modal and drawer share it); the start-of-day look back is NewDayRecap.
responsibility: Recap line and the quiet list of tasks completed today with their time (no archived, nothing from earlier days)
"Noch nicht erledigt": Offen, Jetzt and Wartet as plain rows (not draggable, not links), carry-over dots, the #99 triage block (compact) for Offen/Jetzt past the threshold
One muted line under the list when something is in Jetzt: "Fertig" puts it back to Offen (the move itself lives in useDayClose.finish)
Closing line chosen by local date

Emits `smaller` so the host can close and open the task sheet; Delete goes through useTaskDeletion. The board's gap sits behind the modal, so a deleted row is answered here by one line ("Im Papierkorb", "Rückgängig") until its window ends (#422)

name: DayCloseDialog
description: Optional, quiet closing step for the day (#98): what got done, what is not done yet, a closing line and a copyable summary.
usage: Mounted once in pages/tasks.vue; opened through useDayClose().open() (Mehr panel row, the Erledigt CTA, command palette). Hosted by ResponsiveOverlay (modal at >=768px, drawer below; the same shell as TaskSheet, but not route-bound). The footer markup exists once and has no per-variant look: the theme floor makes both buttons 44px on a phone (Fertig, the one primary, `lg`: 48px) and desktop keeps `md` / `lg` (#551, #552).
avoid: Not for a plain confirmation (UModal, ResponsiveOverlay) and not the first-start-of-day recap (NewDayRecap).
responsibility: Shell only: title, scrolling body (DayCloseBody), footer "Zusammenfassung kopieren" (neutral, first) and "Fertig" (primary, last)
Escape, overlay click and swipe down only close the dialog: nothing is archived, moved, deleted or stored
"Fertig" is the one action with an effect: it stops the timer of the Jetzt task and moves it back to Offen (useDayClose.finish)

Copy writes plain markdown in the UI locale to the clipboard; the button itself confirms ("Kopiert" with a check for 3 s, width kept by stacking both icon + label states) and an in-dialog live region announces it; failures go through useErrorHandler
"Make smaller" closes the dialog first, then opens the task sheet with the title in edit mode (never modal on modal)
Focus returns to the trigger, or to the board when the trigger is gone (palette)

name: DayCloseTaskRow
description: One "not done yet" row in the closing step (#98): title, column label, carry-over dots, and the optional triage actions.
usage: <DayCloseTaskRow :task="task" @smaller="..." /> inside a <ul> (renders an <li>). Not draggable, not a link.
avoid: Not a board card (TaskCard) and not draggable or a link; only the "not done yet" rows of the closing step.
responsibility: Show the column label (Offen, Jetzt, Wartet) and the #99 dots when the card has been carried over
Offen/Jetzt past the #99 threshold: TaskCarryOverTriage in `compact` mode; Wartet never (the block renders nothing there)
Delete goes through useTaskDeletion (upstream-aware, undo in the row's place, see DayCloseBody); Make smaller is emitted to the host

name: FocusOverlay
description: The layer that calms the board while a task sits in Jetzt (#394): a soft radial pool of warm dusk centred on the Jetzt card (a desk lamp), with a flat defocus under the whole layer.
usage: First child of `.board` in Board.vue, rendered only while the focus is possible (`focusEnabledNow`)
avoid: A calming layer, not a modal backdrop (ResponsiveOverlay) and never interactive; only while a task sits in Jetzt.
responsibility: Two sibling layers, tint and blur, each fading on its own: an ancestor with opacity is the backdrop root and would stop `backdrop-filter` from seeing the board
Measures `#column-progress .task[data-current]` per frame while it is visible or fading, so the pool follows the card (page scroll on the phone, resize, a new card)
Never takes a pointer event, except on touch where it swallows the tap that dismisses it
`aria-hidden`: purely visual, no DOM of the board is removed. Layer rules and gradient: board-focus-overlay.css

Lit above it: only the Jetzt column (header and card, which lifts with `--shadow-task-lifted` while the overlay is visible), and on the phone the nav pill. The Erledigt footer sits below it (#503); on desktop the app bar (z 40) stays above it, undimmed (#694), and the overlay is `fixed` over the whole viewport. While it is lit a classic scroll bar takes the dusk tone. `--focus-dusk` is used only here and in that shadow, never as text, fill or border

Accepted contrast trade-off (DESIGN.md "Receding Text"): the dimmed board is intentionally below 4.5:1 while the overlay is on. Measured 2026-10-29 from composited colours without the blur: worst case muted text on paper at the rim 3.13:1 (3.24:1 on a card, body text on a card 5.7:1); the lit Jetzt column keeps its normal contrast. #503 puts the Erledigt footer under the same trade-off (same rule, same reversal); the app bar is no longer dimmed (#694). It is reversible (mouse move, tap, the Fokus setting); `tests/e2e/a11y.spec.ts` exempts exactly what it covers
Never covers a focused control (a key press hides it, WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.11), never changes drop collision, and the Jetzt card stays laid out at its real size

name: NewCardFlow
description: Guided in-card adding of a task in Offen (#649): the add slot's box becomes a card that takes the title, then asks Thema, Aktivität, Timebox and Notiz one after another and saves at the end. No sheet, no route change.
usage: Mounted by AddTaskSlot (Offen) in place of the sheet; emits `saved` with the new task's id, or `cancel`
avoid: Only in-card adding to Offen; add-and-start in Jetzt, editing and source fields use the sheet's TaskForm.
responsibility: Local state only (title, topic, activity, timebox, notes, step): it does not use `useTaskDraft`, which belongs to the sheet (draft card, spotlight, /tasks/add); saves through `useTaskSync().createTask` in the default source (`useAddTarget`), steps follow that source's fields (`fieldsForSource`); a step with nothing to offer is skipped

The face is the real TaskCard (`draft`), so the saved card and the cue behind the wash match by construction; the topic row exists only once a topic is picked (the title steps down then, as on a card)

Title step (no wash): the field is a textarea that grows with the title (#665; Enter confirms, line breaks become spaces, at most as tall as the face's title, which is what the card shows of it (a long title is clamped there), then it scrolls) and stands where the face's title stands: on the card body padding, or below the topic row once a topic is picked (measured from the face, #668: going back with a topic must not overlap it). The face's own title is hidden there, so the field is the only text; it keeps the field's right padding so both wrap alike. The confirm check is centred vertically on the card, on the line where the answer rows of the later steps stand, so the button controls keep one height; the field keeps the check's width clear (accepted: a short title wraps a few characters earlier)

Steps (one question at a time, over the card): head on the card padding (back left, question, skip right; none on Notiz), then the answers in a 2×2 grid (kd#16): Thema and Aktivität `[1] [2] / [3] [Mehr 4]`, Timebox `[1] [2] / [··· 3]`; the pills carry the name and the key cue only (a topic's mark shows in the list and on the face), a long name is cut with an ellipsis (half the row, not a third). The grid makes the steps about 20 px taller than the title card: the face's min-height is derived from the head, two control rows and the room under them (`--ncf-control-h`, `--ncf-grid-top`, `--ncf-grid-bottom`). Notiz is an input plus a check on the vertical centre; Enter saves. The step slides sideways (140 ms) into the next

Behind the steps the face sits under the stack pill's wash (`--stack-wash-*`) and softened (blur, 45 %), a cue that things are received, not text to read. A pick pulses the wash once (the only cue for Aktivität and Notiz, which a card does not show); saving lifts it

Keys: 1/2/3 pick (Timebox: 1/2, and 3 opens "···"), 4 opens Mehr on Thema and Aktivität, Enter skips (saves on Notiz), Esc goes back (cancels on the title step; with a typed title the slot offers "Rückgängig" in a toast, #665), Cmd/Ctrl+Enter saves now with what is entered, from any step once there is a title (#665; announced by `aria-keyshortcuts` and the check's title). Key cues sit inside the buttons (generated content, so the accessible name stays the label), fine pointers only. Tab order is the DOM order; every step change moves focus to the step (Notiz: its input)

A press outside cancels only while the title is blank; a save error keeps the card where it was (Notiz after Enter) with everything entered; the toast after a save is one row (title and Details, #665) so it stays clear of the saved card at 390 px

Mehr (Thema, Aktivität, kd#16): a cell that looks like the input it opens (dashed outline, transparent, search icon, muted "Mehr", key cue 4; hover is a soft fill, never the ink of a value pill). It opens the list (`NewCardOptionList`: popover from 768 px, drawer below) with the search field focused: the values that are not pills (a typed text searches every value, pills too), and a "Neu: „text“" row when no value has that name (any case) and the source allows free values (`fieldsForSource(...).newValues`: Local any text, Notion without commas and at most 100 characters, so the row shows what is created; Todoist none, then search only). Enter picks an exact match, else the first match, else creates (a partial match never creates by accident; the Neu row is one ↓ away). A step with no values at all is still skipped; the sheet creates a first topic. The new value is just a pick: Local derives topics from tasks, Notion creates the select option on the write (`NotionIntegration` writes the property's own type)

"···" (Timebox) and the lists: ↑/↓ (wrapping) walk field and options, Home/End jump between options (caret keys inside the field), Enter/Space pick, Esc closes (kd#15; plain buttons with one shared handler, not UDropdownMenu: the drawer has no menu primitive and the key-4/3 focus flow (#685) stays). Motion is instant under prefers-reduced-motion
Accepted: unsaved input is lost when the page is left (the card saves only at the end, as the story asks); activity and note have no place on a card, so the pulse is their only cue

name: NewCardOptionList
description: The list behind "Mehr" (Thema, Aktivität, kd#16) and "···" (Timebox) of the guided new-card flow: the values that are not pills, with a search field and a "Neu: „text“" row on Thema and Aktivität
usage: Inside NewCardFlow's popover (desktop) and drawer (phone); the parent owns open/close, the picks and the focus hand-back
avoid: Only inside NewCardFlow's popover or drawer; the task sheet's property pickers use TaskPropertySelect.
responsibility: Search (Thema, Aktivität): the text filters every value of the step, pills included; a "Neu" row shows when no value has that name (any case) and the source allows free values (`newValues`, the source's rules clean the text: Notion turns commas into spaces and cuts at 100 characters, so the row shows what would be created); without free values the field only searches

Enter in the field: a value named exactly as typed (any case) is picked, else the first match, else the text is created (a partial match never creates by accident: the "Neu" row is the first stop of ArrowDown, or a tap); no match shows "Keine Treffer gefunden." (a status line)

Keys: ↑/↓ (wrapping) walk field, "Neu" row and options; Home/End jump between options only while focus is not in the field (there they move the caret); handled keys stop here so no surrounding handler sees them (kd#15). Digits typed in the field never reach the step's 1-4 keys (the parent ignores keys while the list is open)
Options are `ChoiceChip` rows (native buttons) with one shared handler (not UDropdownMenu: the drawer has no menu primitive, kd#15)

name: SortableTaskWrapper
description: Per-item sortable wrapper for dnd-kit. Each task card in a column is wrapped in this component so it can be dragged and sorted within/across columns.
usage: Wraps every task card of a sortable column (BoardColumnItem)
avoid: Only for task cards in a sortable column; static lists (trash, recap, day close) render the card without it.
responsibility: Register with dnd-kit's DragDropManager via useColumnSortable
Expose isDragging state for placeholder styling

Name the card for assistive tech: role=group + aria-label = task title + localised role description. Not role=button: axe's label-content-name-mismatch (WCAG 2.5.3) would demand the whole visible card text in the name.
Enter on the focused card opens the task details (Space starts the keyboard drag); a held key's repeats do not

Delete or Backspace on the focused card deletes it with undo (#579): the shared deleteTaskWithUndo, focus on the neighbour card. Ignored for a held key, a modifier, a drag in progress and keys that bubble from a control inside the card
Preserve data-task-id attribute for E2E tests and CSS targeting
Describe a member of an expanded stack for assistive tech: a visually hidden "n of m in <group>" wired by aria-describedby (#154). The accessible name stays the task title.
Mark a member of an expanded stack with data-from-stack="<group key>" (#147): a click on it is not an outside click for the column's expanded stacks

name: TaskDraftCard
description: Representative card for the task being added in the sheet (#110): empty and white at first, fills live as the form is filled in
usage: Rendered by AddTaskSlot in the same box as the add button while `useTaskDraft` has a draft for that column (Offen, or Jetzt for add-and-start, #125)
avoid: Not a saved task (TaskCard); shown only while a task draft exists in the add slot.
responsibility: Reuses TaskCard for the layout so the draft matches the saved card (regular size; in Jetzt it shows the running time)
Not interactive, not draggable, not part of the tasks store
Looks like a normal card; the spotlight (#96/#102) fades the other cards while the draft is open

name: ElementPickerBar
description: Chrome of the feedback element picker (#227): a hover outline with a name chip around the candidate element and a small hint bar at the bottom centre. Exists only while picking; it is not a toolbar.
usage: Mounted once in pages/tasks.vue next to FeedbackDialog. The picking itself lives in useElementPicker.
avoid: Chrome of the feedback element picker only; not a general highlight or tooltip.
responsibility: Outline and chip follow the candidate (`pointer-events: none`, so they never take a pick)
The hint bar carries the keys and a cancel button; a live region announces "<Komponente>, <Selektor>"
All picker UI is marked `data-feedback-picker`, so its own events pass the picker's capture listeners

name: FeedbackAnnotator
description: The annotate step of the feedback dialog (#247, ADR 014): the native snapshot on a canvas with three tools (Rechteck, Pfeil, Schwärzen), undo last, clear all, and the toggle "Aufgabentexte schwärzen".
usage: Rendered by FeedbackDialog for `step === 'annotate'`; the strokes live in `useFeedback` (module memory).
avoid: Only the annotate step of FeedbackDialog; not a general drawing surface.
responsibility: Pointer drawing: client coordinates are mapped to bitmap pixels through `getBoundingClientRect` because the canvas is CSS-scaled to the modal; a redaction is an opaque fill, no blur
Tool buttons carry icon and name (typography over decoration) with `aria-pressed`; the canvas is `role="img"` with a text alternative that names the number of marks
Drawing needs a pointer; the keyboard path is to leave the step ("Zurück") or rely on the default mask

name: FeedbackDialog
description: In-app feedback (#227, Direction A; screenshot #247): one UModal, three steps. Form (title, description, optional element, optional screenshot, automatic context line), the annotate step (only after a capture), then "Prüfen und senden", which shows exactly what is sent.
usage: Mounted once in pages/tasks.vue; opened from the command palette through useFeedback().open() (desktop only).
avoid: Desktop feedback flow only; other dialogs use ResponsiveOverlay or UModal.
responsibility: Form: title (required, ≤ 120), description (≤ 4000), "Element auswählen" (hides the dialog while picking), draft discard
Screenshot: "Screenshot hinzufügen" hides the dialog while the window is captured, then opens the annotate step
Review: the exact issue body and image, each context item removable; the primary action is the only way anything leaves
With a feedback token whose user may write to the repo: "Als Issue senden"; otherwise (absent, rejected, read only): "Auf GitHub öffnen" with a prefilled link

The repository is public: the form says the report becomes a public GitHub issue, and on the browser path (no token) that sending needs the user's own GitHub account; the review intro repeats both. After the link opens, a toast on the board says to paste the screenshot (clipboard) and send the issue there
Calm inline errors with "Erneut versuchen"; the draft survives every one of them
Escape/X close and keep the draft; focus returns to the board (the palette is gone)

name: FeedbackImage
description: Shows a screenshot of the feedback dialog on a `` (#247, ADR 014). The image only ever lives in an `ImageBitmap`; it is never turned into an `` with a blob or data source, so the CSP keeps `img-src 'self'`.
usage: <FeedbackImage :bitmap="flat.bitmap" :label="t('feedback.screenshot.previewFinal')" />
avoid: Canvas preview of the feedback screenshot; for ordinary images use a plain img.
responsibility: Draws the bitmap (and optional marks) at its own pixel size; CSS scales it to the width of the dialog
`role="img"` with a text alternative from the caller

name: AppNav
description: The global app bar (#470, ADR 017): the `kan-do` wordmark (outside any pill, #642), one pill with the two places (Heute, Statistik) plus, on a page behind ⋯, that page as a third segment (#583), then a separate round ⋯ pill that opens the Mehr panel
usage: Mounted once in app.vue before <NuxtLayout>, so it survives page transitions; hidden on routes with `appNav: false`
avoid: Mounted once in app.vue; secondary pages go behind MorePanel, in-page switching is not a job for the app bar.
responsibility: Brand (#642): the wordmark link sits first in the group, left of the pill and outside it, on the paper veil; DOM and tab order unchanged (brand, Heute, Statistik, third, ⋯). Not shown on a phone (kd#24: it has no backing and printed over the cards scrolling under the bar; Heute links to /tasks)
Desktop (≥768px): sticky bar at the top, the group centred. Phone: the same pills float at the bottom (assets/css/app-nav.css)

Separation from the content behind it (#615, DESIGN.md "The Glass Chrome Rule"): the two pills are frosted glass and a paper veil sits behind them (`.app-nav::before`, no pointer events, so the `.titlebar` drag strip and the page stay usable). Near-opaque fallback without `backdrop-filter` and under reduced transparency. Recipe: `--nav-glass-*` in app-nav.css. The page header is not sticky, so the bar is the only thing that stays

Selected state is a pure function of the route (useAppNav): Heute on /tasks*, Statistik on /statistics, the third segment (Papierkorb, Einstellungen) on /trash and /settings*. ⋯ is never selected and carries no aria-current. An open panel is an overlay, not a navigation: the place keeps its chip, ⋯ shows only a soft "open" fill and aria-expanded

Third segment (#583, DESIGN.md "App bar"): grows in the pill when a page behind ⋯ is entered, shrinks away when Heute or Statistik is chosen, re-measures when Einstellungen <-> Papierkorb. MorePanel leaves out the row of the page the pill shows. One 420 ms timeline (`--nav-move`, `--nav-ease` in app-nav.css, 0 under reduced motion) drives the segment and the phone segment padding; a retarget mid-move continues from the current width. The grey pill is content-sized, so its width follows the segment frame by frame on that same timeline (#616); the segment's left margin runs -gap -> 0 with it, so the pill's 1px flex gap does not step in at the first frame or out at the last. The move starts on the second animation frame after the route change, not at the DOM patch (#643): the first frame lays out and paints the new page and, on a slow main thread (WKWebView, a big board), can outlast the whole 420 ms, which left a timeline started before it already over (segment and pill jumped to the end). Until then the segment holds its start state by inline style, and the phone `has-third` class (padding transitions) flips with the move so all three share one start. Direct load and the first paint show the segment without motion

One indicator (the raised white chip) behind the selected segment: two springs chase the live box of the `aria-current` segment (useNavIndicator, lib/navSpring.ts). `data-moving` on the nav is set until chip and layout are idle (E2E waits on it)
A failing source puts a status dot on ⋯ (error for broken, else warning) and the accessible name says so; the panel explains it
Tag abschließen: closes the panel, returns focus to ⋯, then opens the dialog, so the dialog's return target is ⋯ and not a removed row
Phone: fades out and ignores pointers while a card is dragged (no drop target is covered); the pills and the veil fade, not `.app-nav` itself, so the blur does not pop in at the end (#631)
Desktop ⋯ tooltip "Mehr" (+ "Befehle ⌘K" on the board, where the palette is mounted); no tooltip on touch

name: MorePanel
description: Content of the Mehr popover behind the app bar's ⋯ (#470): the board controls and the pages that are not places
usage: Rendered inside the UPopover of AppNav; reads stores and composables only, no props
avoid: Only the popover behind AppNav's ⋯; the places (Heute, Statistik) are the pill's segments, not rows here.
responsibility: Order on the board: Ansicht (Karten stapeln + group-by chips) -> Tag abschließen -> Papierkorb (n), Einstellungen, App-Update -> sync footer
Ansicht and Tag abschließen exist only while the board is the current place; the rest and the sync footer on every page

The page the pill shows as its third segment (#583: Einstellungen on /settings*, Papierkorb on /trash*) is not listed here; the row returns when the page leaves the pill. App-Update stays on /settings/updates (a different page). The panel closes on every route change, so a row never appears or disappears while it is open
App-Update only in the desktop app (`isTauri()`, absent in the web build, never disabled)
Sync footer: a failing source shows its worst problem (title, hint, "Verbindung reparieren") above "Jetzt synchronisieren" + last sync; silent while every source is healthy

While a sync runs (manual or background) the row's second line reads "Wird synchronisiert…" (spinner from the button's `loading`), so the accessible name carries the state, and a sibling `role="status"` announces it (#647)

Board, desktop only: "Befehle" with the palette shortcut hint opens the command palette (U7 of kd#17: the hint was tooltip-only; the palette has no phone entry). AppNav closes the panel and returns focus to ⋯ first, like `dayClose`
Keyboard: ↑/↓ move focus to the previous/next enabled control (clamped, no wrap), Home/End to the first/last; Tab order and roles stay (a popover, not role=menu)
Emits `close` when a navigation row is chosen and `dayClose` for "Tag abschließen": AppNav closes the panel and returns focus to ⋯ first, then opens the dialog

Reads a mapping saved before #617 (urgent/high/medium/low) through `normalizePriorityMapping`
The first option of a level is what kan-do writes back to Notion
Validates the mapping and emits it on save

`reset()` restores the form as it was on first open, also when no mapping is stored (#627)

Validates mapping configuration
Provides save functionality for completing setup

description: Step for entering and validating a Notion API token
usage: Used in the Notion setup wizard as the initial step

responsibility: Collects and validates Notion integration token
Provides feedback on token validity
Manages token input state and validation process
Offers links to Notion integration setup

name: NewDayRecap
description: "Kurzer Rückblick" (#385, #451, #44): the recap on the first start of a new day, shown over the dimmed board. A still-open deck and a done deck like the board's Offen → Erledigt, and one submit panel with the switch "Erledigte archivieren" and the button "Weiter zum Board".
usage: Mounted once in pages/tasks.vue next to DayCloseDialog; opened by useNewDayRecap().check() on mount. Hosted by ResponsiveOverlay (modal at >=768px with both decks side by side, bottom drawer below with a switcher that shows one deck at a time), the same shell as DayCloseDialog. The page itself never scrolls; only the body may, on very short windows.
avoid: Only the first start of a new day; closing the day is DayCloseDialog.
responsibility: Shell only: headline (title slot), summary (description slot), decks (body), submit panel (footer, pinned)
Escape, scrim click, swipe down and the button all call `leave()`, which follows the switch (#44); the desktop close button is off

Phone switcher ("n noch offen" / "n erledigt", a `UTabs` pill: `role="tab"`, `aria-selected`): one RecapDeck mounted at a time, starts on "noch offen" (on "erledigt" when nothing is open, then without a switcher)
The decks never change size (RecapDeck), so nothing moves while they are looked at
The switch writes `day-recap-store.archiveDone` at once
Dialog semantics, focus trap and the inert board: reka's dialog plus `pages/tasks.vue`; focus starts on the button, `finishLeave()` after the leave hands focus to the board
Submit panel: switch left and button right in a container query (`@md`), stacked when narrow

name: RecapDeck
description: One group of the new-day recap (#385, #451): the finished or still-open tasks as a swipe deck. The front card shows with up to two layers peeking behind it; swiping, tapping, ←/→ or the chevrons send it to the back. The deck never changes size, so nothing on the page moves while it is looked at.
usage: Rendered by NewDayRecap, kind `undone` (left) and kind `done` (right). The parent skips the `undone` group when it is empty; the `done` group is always rendered and copes with an empty list itself (counter "0 / 0", no card, chevrons and keys inert, not a tab stop), as it does with a single card.
avoid: Only inside NewDayRecap; a plain list of tasks uses DayCloseTaskRow rows.
responsibility: `hideHeading`: the heading row turns visually hidden (still the section's name) when the phone switcher already says which deck it is (#44)
Layout: heading row (`min-h-10`, `h2` above the cards), the deck (card height + 1.25rem, whatever the card content or n), the bar (chevron, counter "1 / n", chevron)
Cards are view-only: inert, hidden from the accessibility tree, no task sheet. Front card = newest completion (done) or Jetzt/Offen first (undone)

With 2+ cards the deck is one tab stop: `role="group"`, `tabindex="0"`, roledescription "Stapel", name "{label}, mit Pfeiltasten wechseln"; ←/→ act only while the deck itself has focus. With 0 or 1 card there is nothing to switch to (#478): no `tabindex`, no roledescription, the name is just "{label}"; all three follow `canMove` when the count crosses 1 <-> 2
A visually hidden polite live region announces "2 von 4: Titel" after a settled change (the cards are inert, so this is how a screen reader hears the front card); the counter is decorative
Geometry: layer d (max 2) at `translateY(d*8px) scale(1 - d*0.04)`, deeper cards hidden; front card follows the pointer with `rotate(dx/24 deg)`

Motion (#690): the travelling card (next: front, prev: back) slides sideways 50% of the deck width at full opacity (130ms), then takes its new depth, so it passes behind the stack (next) or comes to the front (prev); settle 240ms `cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)` on transform. Nothing fades out; a card deeper than layer 2 stays visible while it travels. With prefers-reduced-motion cards swap at once (the drag still follows the pointer)
The grab area carries `data-vaul-no-drag`: on phones the deck sits in a drawer, and a card swipe must never drag it closed (closing archives the done tasks, #44)
Gesture, queue and timers live in `useSwipeDeck` (drag past 80px or tap = next, 6px tap slop, queue of 8)
Accepted trade-offs (#451): one card at a time, no list view; two chevrons per deck stay focusable (six tab stops for two decks) so keyboard users need not discover the arrow keys

name: DataBackupList
description: The "Sicherungen" section of /settings/data (#224, ADR 011): when the last backup was taken, "Jetzt sichern", and the backups newest first with their kind, origin and task count. Mostly text; the only colour is the orange line when a daily or manual backup failed. Restoring is requested through an event, the page owns the single confirmation modal.
usage: <DataBackupList @restore="onRestore" />
avoid: Only the Sicherungen section of /settings/data.
responsibility: Loads the list on mount and after every backup; empty, loading and error states
Newest 8 visible, "Alle n anzeigen" for the rest
Unreadable files are listed as "nicht lesbar" without an action; a backup from a newer app version shows a disabled "App aktualisieren"
"Wiederherstellen" follows `restoreBlock`: off with a one-line reason in a conflict, a newer-schema file or an unavailable folder; on in a corrupt file, where restoring is the way out

name: DataConflictCopies
description: The "Konflikt-Kopien" section of /settings/data (#224, ADR 011): files a sync client left next to the data file (Dropbox "conflicted copy", iCloud `kan-do-data 2.json`, Syncthing `.sync-conflict-`) that parse as a data file. Only rendered when there are any. Nothing is ever deleted: "Wiederherstellen" runs the restore flow with that file as the source, "Ablegen" moves it into `backups/` so the sync client stops showing it.
usage: <DataConflictCopies @restore="onRestoreCopy" />
avoid: Only the Konflikt-Kopien section of /settings/data.
responsibility: Lists each copy with its time and task count
"Ablegen" files it away and reports a failure inline

name: DataConflictModal
description: The whole-file choice when the data file was changed elsewhere (another device, a hand edit, a sync client) (#224, ADR 011). It shows exactly two versions with time, device and task count and lets the user keep mine or load theirs; both versions end up in `<folder>/backups/`. With no unsaved changes of mine it collapses to one action, "Neu laden".
usage: <DataConflictModal v-model:open="conflictOpen" /> inside DataStorageNotice (once per page)
avoid: Only for a data file changed elsewhere; other confirmations use DataRestoreModal or a plain UModal.
responsibility: "Später" / Escape keeps the conflict: status and notice stay, writes stay blocked, the app keeps working
"Diese Version behalten": their file goes to backups as `conflict`, then mine is written
"Andere Version laden" / "Neu laden": my state goes to backups as `unsaved`, then the window reloads on their file; a failed backup stops the reload and shows the error inline
Disables the choice that would be unsafe: keeping mine over a newer-schema file, loading an unreadable one

name: DataExportImport
description: The "Daten exportieren / importieren" section of /settings/data (#224, ADR 011): a plain JSON file, independent of the data folder and without any credentials. Export writes through the native save dialog (web, #238: a browser download); import validates the picked file first and then asks the page to confirm (same modal as a restore; web: file chooser).
usage: <DataExportImport @import="onImport" />
avoid: Only the export/import section of /settings/data.
responsibility: "Exportieren…": save dialog, then the current state; cancel changes nothing
"Importieren…": open dialog, validation errors inline (invalid, not a kan-do file, newer schema), on success emits the preview for the confirmation modal

name: DataFolderChangeModal
description: Modal for switching the desktop data folder after the native picker returned a folder (#222, ADR 008). The target decides the choices: an empty folder gets "copy my data here" (the old file stays), a folder that already holds data offers "use the data already there" (the app reloads) or "replace it with my data" (explicit confirm step). Unwritable and unreadable targets are refused inline.
usage: <DataFolderChangeModal v-model:open="open" :choice="choice" />
avoid: Only for switching the desktop data folder.
responsibility: Shows the target path and what is in it; Cancel or Escape changes nothing
Calls `useDataFolder().applyFolder`; Rust flushes pending writes before the switch
Keeps one dialog: replace asks for confirmation inside the same modal (no modal on modal)

name: DataRestoreModal
description: Confirmation with a preview for every action that replaces the data file with another version: restoring a backup, restoring a conflict copy, importing a JSON file (#224, ADR 011). It exists for the comparison (source vs. now), not as an "are you sure?"; the replace is reversible through the `pre-restore` backup the app takes first.
usage: <DataRestoreModal v-model:open="open" :request="request" @after:leave="restoreFocus" />
avoid: Only for actions that replace the data file; other confirmations use a plain UModal.
responsibility: Shows what will be restored and the task counts of the source and of now
Web import (#238): optional default-checked "safety download" of the current data, passed to `request.run`
Runs `request.run`; the window reloads on success, so there is no toast
Shows a failure inline and changes nothing; Cancel or Escape changes nothing

name: DataStorageNotice
description: Persistent single-line notice for the desktop data file (#222, ADR 008; #224, ADR 011). Shown for every state other than `ok`, for cloud-sync conflict copies and, last, for a data file iCloud has not uploaded (#271); it disappears on its own when the state is healthy again. Not a toast: it stays until the problem is gone, except the cloud notice, which "Ausblenden" hides for the rest of the app session (#289, memory only). Also hosts the conflict modal and opens it once when a conflict appears.
usage: <DataStorageNotice /> above the board in pages/tasks.vue, <DataStorageNotice :show-details="false" /> on /settings/data
avoid: A persistent notice for the data file; transient results use a toast, a source's sync problem uses the sync popover.
responsibility: Warning colour for read-only, missing-file, conflict and conflict copies (needs attention); neutral colour for a late iCloud upload in any state (uploading, pending, error: one copy, the data is safe locally); error colour for write-failed and an unavailable folder
`role="status"` so the change is announced politely
The cloud notice is held back (or kept) while a board drag runs, so it never shifts the board under a dragged card
"Details" link to /settings/data (hidden on that page); "Ausblenden" on the cloud notice only; "Lösen" for a conflict; "Erneut versuchen" for an unavailable folder

name: DisconnectSourceDialog
description: Confirmation for taking an integration off the board (#320, epic #264 section 1). States how many tasks leave, where new tasks go when the source was the default, and what happens to changes the source does not hold yet.
usage: <DisconnectSourceDialog v-model:open="open" :source="'notion'" @disconnected="..." />, opened from the Notion settings page now and from the "Verbindungen" page (#324).
avoid: Only for taking an integration off the board; deleting tasks has its own undo, not a dialog.
responsibility: Reads the plan from `useSourceConnections().disconnectPlan` (live) and calls `disconnectSource`
Offers "Erst synchronisieren, dann trennen" only while the source can be reached; "Trotzdem trennen" and "Abbrechen" always
Stays open and says why when the disconnect did not happen (changes left unsynced, Keychain refused)

name: GithubTokenRow
description: One GitHub token entry on /settings/github: purpose, required access and the state area (empty, checking, saved, rejected, error). Flat section, no card (DESIGN.md sub-page pattern).
usage: <GithubTokenRow entry="github-updates" />
avoid: Only the GitHub token entries on /settings/github; the Notion token is TokenStep.
responsibility: Show the state of one Keychain entry: only the last four characters are ever visible
Paste, check and store a token ("Speichern"), re-check it ("Testen"), remove it with undo ("Entfernen")
Keep focus on the field after remove and on the remove button after undo

name: SettingsSubpageLink
description: One quiet link row from a settings surface to a settings sub-page (#242): icon, label, muted description and a trailing arrow. Text weight, no card, no accent colour. Laid out like a connection row of /settings (icon column, gap-4, base-size title; #683): the row sits `-mx-2 px-2` so the icon lines up with the rows above and the hover fill still has room around the text.
usage: <SettingsSubpageLink to="/settings/github" icon="i-ph-key" :label="t('settings.subpages.github.label')" :description="t('settings.subpages.github.description')" />
avoid: Only a link row to a settings sub-page; links to external pages are ExternalLink.
responsibility: Render a single NuxtLink whose accessible name is label + description
Hover and keyboard focus use the standard ink focus ring
Re-emit the click so a host (e.g. a modal) can close itself while the link navigates

name: SourceRow
description: One connected task source on the "Verbindungen" page (#324): icon, name with the quiet "Standard" badge, a status line and the actions that source offers. A hairline-divided list item, no card.
usage: <SourceRow v-for="row in connected" :key="row.id" :row="row" @set-default="..." @repair="..." @open-settings="..." @disconnect="..." />
avoid: Only a connected source on the Verbindungen page.
responsibility: Show the badge as text on the default row, "Als Standard festlegen" on every other row

Status line: muted, warning tone for "Verbindung prüfen" (never an error colour, never a toast); the time text is plain, a separate visually hidden live region announces only the warning, so the 30 s refresh of "vor 3 Min." never interrupts a screen reader
Offer repair / settings / disconnect only where the row data allows them (Local has none)
Actions sit right-aligned and wrap under the name on a phone; every button is 44px high there
Every button name contains the source ("Notion als Standard festlegen") so rows are told apart

name: LocalSetupFlow
description: The local setup as page content inside the welcome sheet (#43): pick an empty or a sample board, then confirm
usage: <LocalSetupFlow @back="flow = null" @complete="onLocalDone" /> inside pages/welcome.vue
avoid: Only the local setup on the welcome page; Notion is NotionSetupFlow.
responsibility: Explains that tasks stay on this device and other connections come later

Two radio cards (empty board, sample board) on reka-ui's RadioGroup (the primitive under Nuxt UI's URadioGroup, whose card variant cannot carry the icon and the answer-row look): arrow keys select, one Tab stop (roving tabindex) and one "Los geht's" confirmation; nothing happens on the pick alone
Seeds the task store (empty, or the shared demo board of #527 with carry-over and topic styles), then emits `complete`
Back returns to the choice
Pattern: first-run setup, diverged from the modal wizard; the radio cards follow the welcome page's answer rows

name: NotionSetupFlow
description: The Notion setup as page content inside the welcome sheet (#43): guide rail (md and up) or progress bar (below md) next to the existing wizard steps, Back and the proceed button. No dialog.
usage: <NotionSetupFlow @back="flow = null" @complete="onConnected" /> inside pages/welcome.vue
avoid: Only the Notion setup on the welcome page; reconfiguring later is NotionSetupModal.
responsibility: Hosts WizardController (steps, validation and saving unchanged) in setup mode and drives it: Weiter, Verbinden, Zurück
Back goes one step, from the first step it emits `back` (the choice)
Step changes animate one pane (fade and 14px slide, direction by forward or back), instant under reduced motion
After each step change focus moves to the step heading so keyboard and screen-reader users keep their place
Completion shows a short "Notion ist verbunden" status beat, then emits `complete`
Pattern: first-run setup, diverged from the modal wizard (a process the user stays in); step progress via SetupRail

name: SetupRail
description: Guide rail of a multi-step setup on a page (#43): a vertical rail with one-line help at md and up, a label plus "n / m" and a progress bar below md. Non-interactive: the steps validate in order.
usage: <SetupRail :steps="[{ key, label }]" :current="2" :help="text" :label="t('notion.modal.stepsLabel')" />
avoid: Progress of a multi-step setup page; not a tab bar and not interactive.
responsibility: Shows done, current and todo steps (state in data-state, aria-current on the current one, a screen-reader "done" on finished ones)
Pattern: step progress, new (guide rail). Replaces the dialog stepper of the Notion modal for the welcome page only
Reduced motion: dot, line and bar changes are instant

name: StatsEstimateRing
description: Q3 chart: ring of the timeboxed tasks of the last 8 weeks that ran longer / as planned / shorter, with its legend
usage: Summary of the Q3 tile
avoid: Only the Q3 estimate chart; a generic ring is StatsRing.
responsibility: Ink ramp only: longer = darkest, as planned = 32 %, shorter = 10 %; no status colour
The aria-label and the legend carry the same numbers

name: StatsOutliers
description: Q3 proof: the tasks of the last 4 weeks that overran their timebox most, each opening the task detail
usage: Open Q3 tile, under the patterns
avoid: Only the Q3 proof list on the Statistik page.
responsibility: List up to five completed tasks (title, planned vs. taken time) as buttons
Emit `open` with the task id; the page owns the detail modal

name: StatsPatterns
description: Q3 detail: the ranked estimate patterns as diverging bars with sample size and a next-timebox line
usage: Open Q3 tile
avoid: Only the Q3 detail on the Statistik page.
responsibility: Show the first four patterns, the rest behind "Alle n Muster anzeigen"
Label a pattern by its kind (activity, topic, timebox size, time of day); activity and topic names are user data (`data-private`)
Bars take the ink ramp only: longer than planned = darkest, shorter = 32 %

name: StatsRhythmBars
description: "Wann arbeite ich?" chart (#600): one bar per visible hour (6:00 to 22:00) with the time tracked in it over the last 8 weeks, the 3-hour peak window in the strong ink and the rest one ramp step lighter; or, without data, muted ghost bars
usage: Summary of the work-rhythm tile in StatsTiles, closed (about 20rem wide at `md+`, full width below)
avoid: Only the work-rhythm summary; the open panel is StatsRhythmGrid.
responsibility: Draw the bars from `hours` (seconds per hour, first visible hour first); heights are relative to the busiest hour, an hour without time keeps a hairline
`ghost` draws a fixed muted shape for the first-run state and is hidden from assistive tech
Carry the numbers as text alternative (`role="img"` and an `aria-label` naming the peak window and its share)

name: StatsRhythmGrid
description: Open panel of the work-rhythm tile (#600): a grid of 7 weekday rows (Monday first) x 16 hour columns (6:00 to 22:00) with the average minutes tracked per weekday and hour over the last 8 weeks, in the ink ramp (darkest = most, `bg-muted` = nothing), hour labels every third column and a "weniger ... mehr" legend
usage: Detail of tile 5 in StatsTiles
avoid: Only the open work-rhythm panel; the closed summary is StatsRhythmBars.
responsibility: Colour a cell by its share of the busiest cell (five ramp steps); weekends and days off are empty cells like any other, never marked
`role="img"` with an `aria-label` that names the peak window and the longest weekday; the sentence and rows beside it carry the same numbers as text
Cells shrink to squares at 390px; weekday and hour labels stay

name: StatsRing
description: Hand-built SVG ring (DESIGN.md "Ink ring"): segments share one circle in the ink ramp, a neutral track, an optional tick for the user's usual value. No chart library.
usage: Verdict (in-timebox share), the Q3 estimate ring and the Q4 time donut on the Statistik page
avoid: A ring in the ink ramp only; not a chart library, and topic hues never go into charts.
responsibility: Draw up to six segments (percent of the circle, ramp step) separated by a small gap
Carry the numbers as a text alternative (`role="img"` + `aria-label`); the centre slot is decoration and hidden from assistive tech

name: StatsTile
description: Disclosure tile of the Statistik page (DESIGN.md "Disclosure tile"): a question as heading, one line and a mini chart; it expands in place to its full panel
usage: Q2 to Q4 and the work-rhythm tile (5) in StatsTiles
avoid: Only the disclosure tiles of the Statistik page; a one-question verdict that stays open is StatsVerdict.
responsibility: Heading `<h2>` holding one toggle `<button aria-expanded aria-controls>`; Enter / Space toggles, Esc closes an open tile
Grouped surface by `tone` (semantic tokens only), full width of the grid when open; a `wide` tile is always full width and, closed at `md+`, puts its line left and its chart right (about 20rem, #600)
Summary slot is always shown, the `detail` slot only while open (`v-if`, so a closed tile has no tab stops in its panel)
Without `toggleable` (no timeboxes at all) the heading is plain text and there is no panel
Expose `focus()` so the grid can restore focus after it reorders the tiles in the DOM

name: StatsTiles
description: Q2 to Q4 of the Statistik page: three question tiles in a grid (one column below `md`) that open in place, one at a time, plus the full-width work-rhythm tile "Wann arbeite ich?" (#600) under them, which shares the same open state
usage: Under the verdict in pages/statistics.vue
avoid: Only under the verdict on the Statistik page.
responsibility: Own the page state `open: 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | null` (initial value from the `initialOpen` prop, i.e. `?open=`; never written back, never persisted)

At `md+` render the open tile first (the list is reordered in the DOM, never with CSS `order`, so reading and focus order match the visual order); below `md` the order stays natural. Tile 5 is full width already and always stays last
Q2 to Q4 stay hidden on an empty review; tile 5 is always shown (its first-run state explains that recording has started, #600)
Tile 5 (work rhythm, #600): in its first-run state it has no toggle and no panel
Restore focus to the toggle of the tile that was just toggled (a keyed DOM move can blur it) and scroll its heading into view only if it is off screen
Pick each tile's one-line answer; Q3 without any timebox is a plain heading with no toggle
Q4 detail (#537): one muted line for the time the completion records do not hold (tasks still open, tasks deleted before completion); no line when both are 0
Emit `open-task` when an outlier is chosen

name: StatsTimeSplit
description: Q4 chart: donut of where the time of the last 4 weeks went (completed tasks only), by topic or activity, in the ink ramp, with a legend
usage: Summary of the Q4 tile (top 3 legend rows while closed) and the rows of its open panel
avoid: Only the Q4 time donut; a generic ring is StatsRing.
responsibility: Fold slices beyond four into "Sonstiges" (the lightest step); topic hues stay on the TopicMark before a topic name, never on the chart
Name the numbers in the aria-label of the ring
`rows` mode renders the full legend (time and share per slice) for the open panel

name: StatsTrendBars
description: Q2 chart: eight bars of the in-timebox share per 7-day window, the last window in the strong ink, the others quiet; a window without a value has no bar
usage: Summary of the Q2 tile (small) and its open panel (larger, with value labels)
avoid: Only the Q2 trend chart; its numbers are StatsWeekTable.
responsibility: Draw the bars from `weeks` (oldest first); heights are the share itself (0-100 %) of a track the value label does not eat into
Carry the values as text alternative; the bars are decoration for assistive tech
Value labels only while `labelled` (open tile); eight columns stay across at 390px

name: StatsVerdict
description: Q1 of the Statistik page, always open: one sentence on the last 7 days against the user's own 4 weeks before, one supporting line and a ring of the in-timebox share with a tick at the usual value
usage: Top of pages/statistics.vue
avoid: Only the always-open Q1 of the Statistik page; the other questions are StatsTile.
responsibility: Pick the sentence from `review.state` / `review.verdict` (empty, thin, quiet, three verdict branches); never red, never praise
Show the ring only in the `verdict` state (#687: with too little history a full ring read as an achievement against the headline); its `aria-label` and the line carry the same numbers
Drop clauses that have no data (no timeboxed task now, no usual value) instead of showing zeros

name: StatsWeekTable
description: The numbers behind the Q2 bars: one row per 7-day window, newest first (period, tasks, share in the timebox, time spent, tasks still open at day end)
usage: Detail of the open Q2 tile
avoid: Only the numbers behind the Q2 bars; for task records use TasksTable.
responsibility: List every window, a `–` for a missing value

Day end (#537): the mean number of tasks still in Offen/Jetzt/Wartet at the last count the app saw on each day of the window, from 3 days with a value on; fewer days read `–`, never 0. The count is the last one seen, not an exact closing time (term `day-end`)
Reflow to two lines at 390px (period above, figures below)

name: TasksTable
description: Table displaying task completion records with columns that can be re-ordered
usage: Used in statistics page to show filtered tasks
avoid: Only filtered task records on the Statistik page; board tasks are TaskCard.
responsibility: Display task records in table format
Handle row clicks to open task detail modal
Show empty state when no data available
Keep the horizontal scroll region keyboard-focusable and named

name: SyncWarningModal
description: Warning when the sync of one source returns an empty or a much smaller result; the user confirms or cancels the sync of that source. Names the source (#318)
usage: Mounted once in pages/tasks.vue, opened by useSyncValidation
avoid: Only for a suspiciously empty or small sync result; a broken source is repaired through the sync popover, never a dialog.
responsibility: Show why the result looks suspicious, the stored and fetched task counts and the last merged sync
Emit `action` ('confirm' | 'cancel'); the caller applies or drops the fetched tasks. Closing the dialog is a cancel (`update:open`)

name: AddTargetSwitch
description: The quiet "Speichern in" line in the add sheet's footer: picks the source a new task is saved to (#321)
usage: Registered as the footer `lead` by pages/tasks/add.vue; only shown with 2+ available sources
avoid: Only the add sheet's footer, and only with 2+ available sources.
responsibility: Muted label + value-as-text picker (property-select grammar, no box or fill); the label is aria-hidden, the trigger is announced once as "Speichern in: Notion"
Lists Lokal and every connected source; the default carries "Standard", a source needing attention stays selectable with a heads-up (not an error)
Locked while the save runs, enabled again after a failed save with the chosen target kept
Opens upward: the line sits at the bottom of the sheet

name: DatePickerField
description: Popover calendar picker for task custom date properties. Wraps UPopover + UCalendar. Replaces <input type="date">.
usage: <DatePickerField v-model="field.value" />
avoid: Only custom date properties; other values use TaskPropertySelect or InlineEditable.
responsibility: Show the formatted date as plain text in read mode (or the muted empty CTA when value is null), no icon
Open a UCalendar popover on click
Emit update:modelValue with { start: string } on date select
Provide Löschen and Heute shortcuts in the popover footer

name: TaskCard
description: Displays and manages an individual task card on the kanban board
usage: Used within BoardColumn to render task items with their properties and interactive elements
avoid: The board card; static read-only copies (trash, day close, recap) use their own rows, drafts use TaskDraftCard.
responsibility: Displays task information: the topic first, the title below it (#584), then the footer (timebox chip, source icon, carried-over dots, priority). The activity is not on the card (#584): the sheet, the grouping and the statistics keep it.

Shows the timebox as the progress chip (#388) at the footer start (#584): a light grey chip with the spent share outside Jetzt, a footer-wide bar in Jetzt that grows to the right from the chip's own position; the card has no progress ring (the task sheet keeps its own)
Shows the carried-over dots (#99) for not-done cards, with the numeral only past the dot cap (#584)
Shows the source icon at the footer start on a board with tasks from 2+ sources (#323), the cloud "save pending" icon next to it while the task's source cannot sync (#319)
Manages task timer functionality (for Progress status)
Handles visual states for different task statuses
Done (#124): regular sheet, struck toned title, teal corner check, and the short in-card confirmation after a drop into Erledigt (board store `confirmingTaskIds`)

Done check spring (#611): the corner check springs in once, as the confirmation layer fades out, when a user action (drop, menu, sheet, palette: all set `confirmingTaskIds`) brought the card into Erledigt; never on load, sync or undo; static under reduced motion
Completion burst (#692, DESIGN.md "Earned celebration"): `TaskCompletionBurst` on the same trigger as the check spring, around the card for ~0.9 s; decorative, none under reduced motion
Timebox nudge (#389): a Jetzt card without a timebox shows the in-card question (board store `timeboxNudgeTaskId`); its own content is hidden under it (`task--nudged`, rules in TaskTimeboxNudge)

Opens the task sheet on a click or tap (kd#25, one gesture for every pointer; Enter via SortableTaskWrapper), lifts to the hovered shadow under a hovering pointer; a collapsed stack's cards never open
Provides drag-and-drop styling

`readonly` (#422): the card of a trash entry. Same face, but no task id on the DOM (board selectors never match it), no open gesture and no pointer cursor; a card that came back from an undo plays its grow-back (`task--returning`)

name: TaskCardContextMenu
description: Wraps TaskCard with a context menu for quick task actions. On desktop: right-click opens the menu via the native contextmenu event. On mobile/touch: a 750ms long press opens the menu; moving more than 14px (grace pixels) cancels it so a drag gesture is never interrupted. Keyboard: the ContextMenu key or Shift+F10 on the focused card (its `.task-wrapper`, a parent of this component) opens the menu at the card; on close focus returns to the card (kd#23). If a drag starts while the menu is open it is closed immediately.
usage: Used in BoardColumn to provide right-click / long-press menu on task cards
avoid: Only wraps TaskCard for the right-click / long-press menu; not for stack headers or other rows.
responsibility: Provides context menu with task actions (status, timebox, delete, etc.)
Handles custom timebox modal
Delegates task operations to composables

name: TaskCarryOverDots
description: Carried-over marker (#99): one small dot per board day, shown from day 2 (#121).
usage: <TaskCarryOverDots :day="displayDay" /> in the TaskCard footer; renders nothing on day 1 (and below). `decorative` next to text that already names the count (task sheet).
avoid: Only the carried-over marker (day 2 and later); not a progress indicator.
responsibility: Shows up to CARRY_OVER_DOT_CAP dots; only past the cap a "+" and the muted numeral follow (#584; never in decorative mode)
Names the meaning for hover and screen readers; not a tab stop (kd#27: 8+ extra stops on a board of carried-over cards) ("Tag 3 auf dem Board")
Never interactive: no click handler and no focus, so it adds no drag-vs-click target

name: TaskCarryOverTriage
description: Calm triage block for a card carried over CARRY_OVER_NUDGE_DAYS or more board days (#99): "Still here after N days." with Keep, Make smaller and Delete.
usage: <TaskCarryOverTriage :task-id="id" @smaller="focusTitle" @delete="deleteTask" /> `compact` for list rows that already show the dots (#98): actions only, no wash, no heading, and a quiet look (all three ghost, #551; the task sheet block too, #552) so the block never outweighs the primary of the surface that lists it. Standalone so the closing step (#98) can list it under "still open". Renders nothing when no nudge is due (fewer days, kept recently, Wartet or Erledigt).
avoid: Only on cards carried over several days; not a general card menu (TaskCardContextMenu).
responsibility: Keep: silences the nudge for CARRY_OVER_NUDGE_DAYS further days (store), the dots keep counting
Make smaller / Delete: emitted, the host owns the title field and the sheet lifecycle
Delete copy names the upstream consequence (Notion, Todoist)

name: TaskCompletionBurst
description: The earned celebration of a completion (#692, DESIGN.md "Earned celebration"): a short burst of small teal pieces that flies out of the card's check, around and over the card, and fades.
usage: Rendered by TaskCard while a completion plays (the card decides when); it tells the card when it is over.
avoid: Only the completion celebration, driven by TaskCard; no other success feedback uses it.
responsibility: Draws 24 fixed pieces (6 x 12 px rectangles and 10 px dots, deterministic so screenshots are stable) in the done-teal tints `success-200..500` plus `neutral-400`, flying out along an ellipse of ~175-230 x 88-133 px around the card centre, where the confirmation check shows (#124). Look constants are the round-1 prototype's variant A.

Plays once, 900 ms (a piece may start up to 90 ms late), animates only `transform` and `opacity`, so the card and the board never reflow. It sits above neighbouring cards and takes no pointer events: the next drag works while it plays.

Owns its lifetime: the store flag behind the in-card confirmation ends at 800 ms, the burst runs a little longer. It emits `done` after its last piece ends (a timer is the fallback when no animation event comes).
Decorative: `aria-hidden`, no focus, no text. Reduced motion: the card does not mount it and the CSS hides it.

Pieces extend over neighbouring cards and clip at the edge of the screen: `.board-container` on mobile, `.board` on desktop (board.css, `overflow: clip`), so a card in the right column never grows the page sideways.

name: TaskDeletedGap
description: The slot of a card that was just deleted (#422, UX decision D "Im Papierkorb"): the card's own box, with a trash icon, "Im Papierkorb" and a "Rückgängig" pill centred in it, all in raspberry on a muted raspberry fill without an outline (#581, #57; destructive state, The Status Is Not Decoration Rule), and a draining line along its bottom edge. From #57 the gap is compact (`--task-note-height`, the collapsed Yesterday note's height): the cards below glide up by the difference and back on undo.
usage: Rendered by BoardColumn / BoardColumnProgressContent at the card's slot, from `useTaskDeletion().gaps`; never inside SortableTaskWrapper (a gap is no dnd-kit sortable: not draggable, not droppable, no sheet).
avoid: Only the slot of a just-deleted card with undo; never inside a drag list.
responsibility: Holds a compact slot (`--task-note-height`: 42px, 46px at 390px) for the undo window, for a card and a stack alike; the box glides from the card's measured height (`--gap-from`) to it in 220 ms; the card itself is already out of `tasks`

D6 transition: a non-interactive picture of the card (TaskCard `readonly`, `inert`) shrinks to 0.92 and fades out towards its own centre in 220 ms (ease-out) while the answer layer fades in over the same time; transform and opacity only

Red theme (#581, outline dropped #57): the box carries a muted shape (`::before`: card radius, 12% `error` wash over the page, no border) that fades in with the answer layer (220 ms, opacity only; it clips away with the closing glide). Label and trash icon are `error-700`, the undo pill is `color="error" variant="soft"` (the global compound in `app.config.ts` sets `error-700` text, #594), the drain line is `error-500` (a graphic, 3:1 needed)

Drain line: 2px, full width at the bottom edge (clipped to the radius), 5 s `scaleX` 1 -> 0 from the left, linear; paused with the window while the pointer or focus is inside the gap (two flags, resumed when both are off; resumed on unmount too, `useDeleteHold`)

Window end (`state: 'closing'`): the box glides shut in 280 ms (grid row 1fr -> 0fr, the list gap's negative margin included) and focus moves to the next card, or the list when it was the last, if it was in or lost with the gap
`prefers-reduced-motion`: the picture only crossfades (no scale), the drain line is static, the gap closes without gliding

Contrast: "Im Papierkorb" and the pill text are `error-700` on the 12% wash (earlier figures were measured on 6%; re-measure with the rendered Impeccable scan `npm run design:detect`); the `error-500` drain line is a graphic and needs 3:1

name: TaskDetailContent
description: Shared presentational component for task detail views with inline editing
usage: Used by both TaskDetailModal and pages/tasks/[id].vue
avoid: Shared body of the task detail (modal and page); not for the add form, which is TaskForm.
responsibility: Display task properties as labelled rows (shared with the add form, #161), notes, and custom fields
Every property is a row in a stable position; unset Thema/Aktivität show the empty "Auswählen" state (#161)
Order: property rows (time spent last, with the time left beside it, kd#4), notes, custom properties, metadata (#386). Desktop slideover: the metadata is pinned to the bottom, the rest scrolls
Provide formatted display of all task metadata
Render error state when task not found
Handle inline updates and synchronization

Topic and activity pickers (TopicPropertyPicker): the topic mark before each option, no control inside an option; an edit mode in the picker's footer ("Bearbeiten" / "Fertig") lists one button row per option, and a row closes the picker and opens the shared TopicEditorHost under the property row (#430, #431, #443); topics also get a "Themen verwalten" row
Host the carried-over triage block and line (#99)

Guard against drift (#161, kd#4): at most six always-visible standard rows (Status, Priorität, Thema, Aktivität, Timebox, Aufgewendete Zeit), no per-row icons, no dividers; more always-visible rows must revisit the layout. The one hairline is the pin line above the desktop metadata footer, a boundary of the scroll region, not a row divider

name: TaskDetailCustomFields
description: Custom (Notion) properties of a task as flat label/value rows with inline editing
usage: Used in TaskDetailContent under the "Eigenschaften" heading
avoid: Only the Notion custom properties in the task detail; core properties use TaskPropertyRow.
responsibility: Renders every custom property type (text, number, url, email, phone, checkbox, select, multi-select, date)
Every configured property is a row in a stable position; an empty one shows its empty state ("Auswählen…", "+ hinzufügen") instead of hiding behind a "+ n weitere" action (#161)
Integrates with the property options store for select/multi-select
Emits update events for the parent to handle persistence

name: TaskDetailMetadata
description: Metadata section of the task detail (source, created, id), collapsed by default
usage: Used by TaskDetailContent; last in the flow on mobile, pinned to the bottom of the desktop slideover (#386)
avoid: Only the collapsed metadata section of the task detail.
responsibility: Quiet collapsible with the source, the creation date and the stable task id
`pinned` adds the hairline above it and its padding, so it reads as the sheet footer (the notes sit above, in the scroll region)
The open state is a v-model owned by the parent, so a resize that swaps pinned and in-flow keeps it

name: TaskDetailModal
description: Modal displaying detailed task information
usage: Reusable modal for showing task details
avoid: Only the task detail modal; new code opens tasks in TaskSheet.
responsibility: Display task properties, notes, and custom fields via TaskDetailContent
Handle modal open/close state
Provide delete action with undo capability

name: TaskDetailNotes
description: Notes section of the task detail: rendered Markdown in read mode, a plain textarea while editing
usage: Used by TaskDetailContent; inline in the flow, directly after the property rows and time (#386)
avoid: Only the notes of the task detail; other long text uses a plain textarea.
responsibility: Read mode renders the notes as sanitized Markdown (utils/renderMarkdown); edit mode stays the textarea

Written notes use `interactive-display` so links sit beside the edit trigger, not inside role=button (#208); empty notes have no links and keep the plain trigger. The trigger element is replaced when notes flip empty/written; InlineEditable restores keyboard focus to the new one
Empty notes keep the muted placeholder trigger with the dotted rule; written notes use the soft hover fill (a dotted rule under every rendered line would be noise)
Save with Cmd+Enter (macOS) or Ctrl+Enter, the hint names the key of the current platform

name: TaskForm
description: Form component for creating and editing tasks with integration support
usage: Used in task creation and editing modals, with buttons handled by parent modal
avoid: Only creating and editing a task in the sheet; the in-card flow is NewCardFlow.
responsibility: Provides the same labelled property rows as TaskDetailContent (#161): one grammar for add and detail
Title as a large clean input, properties as label/value rows; Thema/Aktivität are rows with the empty "Auswählen" state
Notes section always visible (no reveal button)
Help text lives in the pickers and as accessible descriptions, not in tooltips

Handles form submission and validation: an empty or whitespace-only title shows an inline error under the title (role="alert", aria-invalid, focus back on the input; clears once the title has text, #662)
Converts between time formats (minutes/seconds)
The timebox input starts empty (`null` minutes = no timebox, muted "—" placeholder), never 0; an empty, zero or negative input means no timebox (#663)
