Emits task data for parent to save to integration
Exposes submitFormExternal method for parent modal footer buttons

name: TaskPriorityBadge
description: Visual indicator for task priority level (low, regular, high; #617)
usage: Used within task cards to display priority status
avoid: Only the three priority levels on a card; statuses are columns, not badges.
responsibility: Displays appropriate priority indicator based on task priority level
Done cards show no priority badge (#124, TaskCard)

name: TaskProgressChip
description: The timebox label of a task card as its progress item (#388)
usage: First item of the TaskCard footer (#584; not on the add sheet's Jetzt draft)
avoid: Only the timebox label of a task card; not for the add sheet's Jetzt draft.
responsibility: Outside Jetzt: a light grey chip "45 min" (track and fill half a step lighter since #584) whose grey fill shows the spent share of the timebox (no colour, also not on overrun or done cards)

In Jetzt: once the card has settled it springs wider (x axis only) into a bar across the whole footer, anchored at its own left edge (the footer start, #584) and growing to the right over the source icon, carry-over dots and priority badge: "12 min ...... 45 min", fill primary, warning above 80 percent
No timebox: a spent-time chip that pops in when the card enters Jetzt and counts forward; outside Jetzt it stays as a quiet grey chip only once time was spent, otherwise there is no label
Reserves its collapsed width in the footer row (hidden sizer), so the carry-over dots are the item that clips in a narrow footer
Starts from the state the task's chip was last rendered in (`lib/timeboxChipMemory`), because a cross-column move mounts a fresh card; a page load with a card in Jetzt shows the bar at once

While its own card is dragged (the card stays mounted as the hidden placeholder, also for a drop back into Jetzt) it counts as out of Jetzt, so it grows again on the drop instead of keeping the bar (#411). The grow starts two frames after the drop: dnd-kit re-inserts the card's node in the drop's own task, and a class flip with no style pass in between has nothing to ease from, so the morph was silent in production builds (#540)
Never owns a timer: it only reads `timeSpentSeconds`, which the app-level driver advances (#352)
Motion is CSS only; `prefers-reduced-motion` shows the end state at once. Never takes pointer events.
The width spring is the app's one spring: it marks the moment a label becomes the card's live status. It never runs on page load; the bar has no shadow, it sits flat on the card's own (#410)

Warning accent in the 600 step: the 500 step measured 2.97:1 on the card surface (below the 3:1 non-text floor, WCAG 1.4.11), the 600 step 4.13:1. Text on every fill keeps 4.5:1 (`a11y.spec.ts`, Jetzt card at 50 %, 85 %, over)
A silent progressbar: the value is the percent, no value text and no live region, so per-second updates stay quiet; without a timebox the name is the spent time and there is no value

Accepted: in Jetzt the bar covers the source icon, carry-over dots and priority badge (TaskCard makes the group after the chip inert); the spring overshoot may poke a few px past the footer padding, inside the card

name: TaskPropertyRow
description: One labelled property row of the task sheet: quiet label left, value right
usage: Detail (TaskDetailContent, TaskDetailCustomFields) and add (TaskForm) share this row, so each property is learned once
avoid: Only labelled property rows of the task sheet; a section title is SectionHeader.
responsibility: Fixed label column (Label role, text-muted) so values line up across rows
Value slot receives `labelId`, so the value control can be named by its label
44px hit area at <=767px; no icon, divider or box (space separates groups)
`private` marks the value (not the label) `data-private`: hidden during a feedback screenshot (#247)

name: TaskPropertySelect
description: Value-as-text picker for a property row (status, priority, topic, activity, select fields)
usage: Value slot of TaskPropertyRow in the detail and add views
avoid: Only a value picker inside a TaskPropertyRow; topic and activity use TopicPropertyPicker.
responsibility: Text-style trigger (USelectMenu `property` variant from app.config.ts), named "<label>: <value>"
Optional help text at the top of the open picker (reachable on touch, replaces tooltips)
Clearing lives inside the picker (a "<label> entfernen" action), never as a × on the trigger
Menu items use Nuxt UI size `md`, the same text size as the task card context menu (text-sm)

Optional `item-leading` slot per option (the topic mark), a `content-top` slot above the search (after the hint; the edit rows of TopicPropertyPicker, #443) and a `content-extra` slot above the clear action ("Bearbeiten", "Themen verwalten")

name: TaskSheet
description: Responsive sheet that hosts the nested task routes (/tasks/:id, /tasks/add)
usage: Mounted once in pages/tasks.vue. `open` is driven by the route; closing animates first, then `after-leave` fires so the host can navigate to /tasks.
avoid: Only hosts the nested task routes; other overlays use ResponsiveOverlay directly.
responsibility: Hosted by ResponsiveOverlay: a slideover (side right) at >=768px and a bottom drawer below; the shell owns the breakpoint, the frozen variant and the open/close echo guard
Focus on open (the drawer: ResponsiveOverlay moves it in, #566), focus trap and focus return come from reka's FocusScope
Detail route: ignores an outside pointer-down in the first moments after it opened: the second click of a double-click on a card lands on the overlay and must not dismiss the sheet (kd#25)
Keeps Escape inside an active inline editor (and the topic editor, #430) from closing the sheet
Falls back to the board when there is no trigger to return focus to (deep link)
After adding a task, focus goes to the saved card instead of the add slot (#125)

name: TaskSourceIcon
description: The source a task belongs to, as a 16px muted icon (#323)
usage: <TaskSourceIcon :source="task.source" /> at the start of the TaskCard footer, only on a board that holds tasks from 2+ sources
avoid: Only on a board with tasks from 2+ sources.
responsibility: Maps a source to its bundled icon (Local `ph`, Notion and Todoist `simple-icons`: no remote fetch, ADR 012)
Names the source for assistive tech ("Lokal", "Notion") and for hover; shows no visible text
Is not focusable and not interactive, so it adds no tab stop and is no drag handle

name: TaskStack
description: A collapsed stack of task cards in a grouped column: front card, peek layers, pill
usage: Used by BoardColumn for a group of 2+ tasks while it is collapsed. Expanding is declarative (#147): BoardColumn stops rendering the stack and renders the group's members as ordinary cards, behind a TaskStackHeader (#148).
avoid: Only a collapsed stack of 2+ tasks; an expanded group renders its members through BoardColumnItem.
responsibility: Shows the group as a front card (the first task) with `min(count - 1, 2)` peek layers behind it (`--stack-layers`, step `--stack-collapsed-offset`), and the details as a split capsule (TaskStackPill, #504: grouping property | stack icon + count) centred on the front card, whose content is muted (#195, #371)
The collapsed face (cards, layers, pill) is one unit, so a whole-stack drag (#150) moves all of it

Is ONE dnd-kit sortable (#150): its id is the front task's id (that card is inert, so the id is unique), its data carries the stack (key, label, taskIds). Dropping it moves every member; the column and useBoardDndKit read the members from the data. The stack root is the sortable element (it includes the pill), the control is its handle

Is one keyboard stop: a role=button control named "<front title>, <group>, <n> Aufgaben", with aria-expanded; Enter and click ask the column to expand (`expand`), Space picks the whole stack up (dnd-kit's keyboard sensor), like a card. Its role description and instructions are stack-specific
Keeps its cards inert: they are neither focusable nor read out, the control is the only way in
Applies the data attributes the board reads (data-task-id = front card, data-stack-task-ids)
`preview`: the face as it rests, for the DragOverlay: no control, no sortable, no click
Marks its root `kando-dnd-dragged` while it is the drag source: assets/css/dnd.css turns it into one grey slot of the stack's footprint (front card greyed, layers and pill invisible)
Its members become individual sortables once the column expands the group (#147)

name: TaskStackHeader
description: Header row of an expanded stack: the stack's pill as its title and a round close button (#578)
usage: Rendered by BoardColumnItem in front of the members of an expanded group (#148)
avoid: Only the header row of an expanded stack; a column's header is BoardColumnHeader.
responsibility: The pill is the same TaskStackPill the collapsed face shows, centred over the card column: on expand it rises from the face to this row, on collapse it sinks back (useStackMotion), so it is one object that moves and never vanishes. Same width cap in both places (94 % of the column, property segment 10rem): nothing here may squeeze it, the close button is positioned outside its width

The round X at the row's right edge asks the column to collapse the group (click, Enter, Space); the column returns focus to the stack, as it does for Escape. Its accessible name is "Gruppe <group> schließen" (no aria-expanded: it is an action). 24px round, same soft grey as the pill, the add-task button and the app bar's ⋯ (`--ui-bg-muted`, no ring); on hover the pointer cursor and one neutral step darker (`--ui-color-neutral-300`: `--ui-bg-accented` is the same value as `--ui-bg-muted` here, so it showed nothing, kd#55); 44px hit area on touch
The root is a role=group named by the stack caption text; it is not a sortable and carries no data-task-id: dnd-kit and the drop mapping never see it
Row min-height 2rem (2.75rem on touch widths)

name: TaskStackPill
description: The face of a collapsed stack's pill (#504): one split capsule, "<property> | <stack icon> <n>"
usage: Inside the aria-hidden pill layer of a collapsed TaskStack, centred on the front card
avoid: Only the face of a collapsed stack's pill inside TaskStack.
responsibility: Left segment names the grouping property the way a card shows it: topic = TopicMark + neutral name (hue only on the mark); priority 1-3 = the real TaskPriorityBadge as the segment itself (no hairline after it); activity, custom/Notion value and the empty group = the plain name
Right segment is the stack icon (`i-ph-stack`) and the count; it never shrinks, a large count widens it only

The property segment is capped at 10rem and truncates with an ellipsis (look decision, tune here); the full name stays in the stack control's accessible name, so there is no tooltip. The pill is decorative: the visible word "Aufgaben" is gone, the control still says it
Soft neutral like the former text pill (`bg-muted`, label role 500 / 0.6875rem, 0.75rem on touch), 1.5rem high, fully rounded outer shape, a 1px hairline between the segments
Never takes a pointer event (its layer is `pointer-events: none`)

name: TaskTimeboxNudge
description: In-card micro dialog (#389) that offers a timebox when a card without one lands in Jetzt
usage: Inside TaskCard (the Jetzt card only); the board store's `timeboxNudgeTaskId` decides which card shows it
avoid: Only the micro dialog of the Jetzt card without a timebox; other prompts are not cards.
responsibility: Non-modal layer over the card face: no focus move, no trap; only its controls take pointer events, so the card stays draggable and a click on the face still opens the sheet (on touch the layer swallows the tap)
One-click presets (15, 30 min) and an inline minutes field (1 to 480); Escape steps back, then dismisses
Auto-dismisses after TIMEBOX_NUDGE_MS; the hairline countdown pauses while the pointer or focus is on the layer or the field is open
Ends itself when the card leaves Jetzt, is deleted, gets a timebox elsewhere or opens its sheet

The card dims its own content through the `task--nudged` class (TaskCard); the rules for both live in this file In-card question pattern (DESIGN.md "Ask in place"; this is its first user, extract a shared layer when a second exists):
One at a time, keyed by task id in a transient board-store flag (a cross-column move mounts the card fresh), set only by user-driven moves: never by page load, sync, undo or closing the day

Covers the card face, does not rearrange it: a radial wash of the sheet colour (the stack pill's wash), the card's content hidden underneath (still in the DOM), answers as soft pills like the stack pill, the question in the Title step
Copy is the question only ("Timebox hinzufügen?"): no title bar, no Abbrechen/OK pair; the answer is the click

`role="group"` named by the question, real buttons after the card's content in DOM order, never `role="dialog"` or `aria-modal`; no announcement and no focus move. Accepted: a keyboard user reaches it by tabbing and has the palette, menu and sheet for the same action
The countdown is a functional animation and stays under reduced motion; fades and the settle do not

name: TopicPropertyPicker
description: The task sheet's Thema / Aktivität picker: the shared TaskPropertySelect plus an edit mode in its footer (#443)
usage: Value slot of the Thema and Aktivität rows in TaskDetailContent
avoid: Only the Thema / Aktivität rows of the task sheet; other properties use TaskPropertySelect.
responsibility: Picking mode is the plain picker (topic mark per option); options carry no control, so the open picker has no button inside a `role="option"` item (axe `nested-interactive`, #430 D6)

"Bearbeiten" (footer) switches the same popover to edit mode: heading plus one real button per option (mark, name, usage count, pencil) replace search, options, "Themen verwalten" and the clear action; the footer then holds only "Fertig"

A row hands the name to the parent (`edit`) and closes the picker; the parent opens the shared topic editor (#430). The row blurs itself first: Reka refocuses the trigger on close only while focus is still inside the content, so the editor keeps the focus it takes itself (no timer)
"Fertig" keeps focus on the same button: the search field that returns does not autofocus until the next open (the Nuxt UI input otherwise takes focus one tick after it mounts)

Edit mode never survives a reopen (reset when the picker opens, not when it closes: see the watch); "Bearbeiten" is hidden for an empty list, and the footer slot is not passed at all when it would hold nothing (empty Aktivität list, #461); `editable` false (add dialog preview) renders the plain picker without edit mode and without "Themen verwalten"
Enter and Space on the rows and the toggle stop at the button: the combobox would otherwise swallow them
Edit list scrolls at about 8 rows; rows are 32px, 44px at max-md (touch target)

name: TopicEditor
description: The one editor every entry point opens (#430, #431): Name, Farbe (nine hues plus none, radio swatches) and Symbol (a button showing the current mark; a popover with 24 glyphs plus none). An activity has the Name only. A name a source owns (Notion schema or any non-Local task) is disabled with the reason; Farbe and Symbol stay editable and say they apply only in kan-do. A new name that already exists merges into it and the target's style stays. Saving is local and immediate: no loading or error state.
usage: Hosted by TopicEditorHost (settings list row, task-sheet picker edit mode)
avoid: The one topic editor, hosted by TopicEditorHost; never a second editor for the same job.
responsibility: Save through `useTopicManagement().rename` (every store, one pass) and `useTopicStylesStore().setStyle`
Name is trimmed; an empty name or nothing changed cannot be saved; the editor closes after saving
The key of the editor is the *name*: the host re-keys after a rename instead of editing the old name
Focus starts in the Name (the first colour when the name is gated); Escape closes the editor only (the task sheet vetoes its own dismissal, `data-topic-editor`)
Hue and symbol groups are `SwatchRadioGroup` (`role="radiogroup"`, arrow keys); the symbol popover closes on pick or Escape and keeps the editor open

name: TopicEditorHost
description: Where the shared TopicEditor appears (#430). At >=768px a muted inline panel under the row it belongs to (settings list row, task-sheet property row); below, a bottom drawer. Opened from inside the task sheet's drawer (`nested`) it is a second, nested drawer: vaul scales the sheet back and its top edge stays visible above the editor ("one thing at a time"); over the settings page it is a plain drawer.
usage: `<TopicEditorHost :key="name" :topic="name" kind="topic" @close="..." @saved="..." />`; the parent re-keys by the name and closes the host on `close` (the editor emits `saved` before `close`)
avoid: Only places the shared TopicEditor (inline panel or overlay); it holds no form of its own.
responsibility: Pick inline or drawer from the viewport; inside the task sheet follow the sheet's own frozen variant (#199)
Keep the drawer open only while mounted; closing it (overlay, swipe, Escape) emits `close`
A drawer unmounted mid-edit (the sheet closes, the viewport crosses 768px) drops the unsaved edit, nothing is saved half-way

name: TopicMark
description: The mark before a topic's name (#431): a 12px hue dot, or the Phosphor fill glyph (16px) in the hue when a symbol is set (muted gray when it has no hue). A topic with neither hue nor symbol renders nothing, so no gap appears and the card looks as it did. Decorative: `aria-hidden`, the name carries the meaning; never a pointer target (the card is a drag item, #430 known issue 4).
usage: Card topic line, the sheet's Thema row, picker options, the settings list, the editor preview, the statistics dialog
avoid: The only place a topic hue appears; never a coloured chip, label or surface, and not in charts.
responsibility: Resolve the mark from the topic name (and the task, for the source colour) through `useTopicColor().markOf`
Or show an explicit `hue` / `symbol` (the editor previews an unsaved choice)
Colour comes from the `--topic-<hue>` tokens (assets/css/main.css) through one custom property, never a palette class

name: TrashEntryRow
description: One deleted task in the trash (#422): the board's own card, read-only, with when it was deleted, where it was and the actions.
usage: Rendered by pages/trash.vue (every entry, restore and remove-forever)
avoid: Only a deleted task on the trash page; live tasks are TaskCard.
responsibility: Shows the standard TaskCard (`readonly`, `preview`: no sheet, no drag, no swipe, no task id on the DOM); a Wartet card is muted as on the board
"Gelöscht vor …", "War in <Spalte>" ("War in Jetzt, kommt zurück nach Offen" for a task from Jetzt) beside the card on desktop, below it at 390px
"Wiederherstellen: <title>" for every entry; "Endgültig löschen: <title>" on the page only (`forever`), the sheet is a one-action surface
The ✕ asks in place (kd#21, aligned with "Papierkorb leeren"): question, "Endgültig löschen", "Abbrechen" (focused); Esc or Abbrechen returns focus to the ✕
A failed restore leaves the entry where it is (`useTrash` reports the error)

name: ChoiceChip
description: The one control for "pick one of a few" (#72): a round answer chip that fills with ink on hover and when picked, or a list row of a searchable option list. The new-card flow's answer pills, the timebox nudge's presets and icon controls and the new-card option rows are this one look.
usage: <ChoiceChip shape="pill" :picked="picked === value" :current="value === current" @click="pick(value)">{{ label }}</ChoiceChip>; `chip` (equal-width preset in a row), `icon` (square-round control, give it an `aria-label`), `row` (full-width option inside a list, `aria-current` marks the current one); `field` makes a pill read as the search field it opens. Native attributes (`disabled`, `aria-*`, `data-testid`) land on the button.
avoid: Not for an action (UButton), not for a toggle that stays on beside others (UButton soft/primary with `aria-pressed`, as the board menu's group-by chips) and not for a property value of the task sheet (PropertyValueTrigger).
responsibility: Render one native `<button type="button">`; the host decides what a click means and sets `picked` (the answer just given: ink fill, pressed in) and `current` (the value already set: a hairline ring)

Shapes carry the geometry each site had: `pill` takes its height from `--choice-chip-h` (the new-card flow sets it to its control height), `chip` and `icon` are 36 px (44 px on a phone and on touch screens), `row` is a 32 px list row (44 px and larger text when `large`, the drawer's)
Ink hover and the picked state ("one lamp": only the answered control is dark); visible focus ring; disabled `chip` and `icon` dim, a disabled `pill` keeps its look and loses the pointer
Key cues (`<kbd>`) and truncation spans are slot content; the host lays them out

name: EmptyNote
description: The one empty state: a muted one-sentence line ("Noch keine X.") for a list, table or panel that fills with use.
usage: <EmptyNote data-testid="trash-empty-state">{{ t('trash.empty') }}</EmptyNote>; spacing comes from the call site's `class`.
avoid: Not for a search or filter without a result beyond the sentence "Keine X gefunden.", not for an error (UAlert) and never for an empty board column, which stays blank.
responsibility: Render the sentence as muted small text, nothing else: no icon, no heading, no action (DESIGN.md "Voice and copy": "Noch keine X.")
Pass attributes (testid, role) and the call site's spacing class through to the paragraph

name: ExternalLink
description: Link to an external page. In the desktop app it opens in the system browser through tauri-plugin-opener (narrow URL permission in src-tauri/capabilities); on web it is a plain `<a target="_blank">`.
usage: <ExternalLink href="https://www.notion.so/my-integrations">Manage token</ExternalLink>
avoid: Only for pages outside the app (opens the system browser on desktop); in-app links use NuxtLink.
responsibility: Keep the href real so middle-click, copy-link and screen readers behave on web
Hand the URL to the opener plugin on desktop instead of navigating the webview
Report an opener failure through useErrorHandler (context `external_link`), never swallow it

name: ListRow
description: One hairline-divided list row (#76): content on the left, trailing actions on the right (the slot's own flex children), no card. The static row holds whatever the slot gives it; the `action` row is one full-width button (open, expand) with the focus ring and a 44 px target.
usage:
…the row's own flex children, trailing buttons last…
; `action` with `@click` for a row that opens something; `#after` holds what unfolds below an action row.
avoid: Not a card (TaskCard, UCard) and not a table row (UTable); a row that is only text with no trailing part is a plain `<li>`.
responsibility: Render the `<li>`; the surrounding `<ul class="divide-y divide-default">` draws the hairlines
`hover` (action rows): `text` (default) or `surface` for rows whose children set their own colours
`density` sets the vertical rhythm: roomy (sources), cozy (action rows), compact (backups)

`action`: the slot (use a `<span class="flex …">` for its layout) sits inside one `<button>` with `focus-ring`, `min-h-11`, `aria-expanded` from `expanded`, `aria-label` from `label`; `focus()` is exposed for hosts that return focus to the row
Attributes (`data-testid`, …) land on the `<li>`; `buttonTestid` names the action button

name: PageHeader
description: Reusable header for settings-style pages with title, description and optional actions; scrolls away with the page (#615)
usage: Used in the sub-page layout for the settings sub-pages (/settings/*); not on /settings, /trash and /statistics (`pageHeader: false`, #670, #686): the app bar names those, the layout renders the title as a screen-reader-only h1
avoid: Only the settings sub-pages; /settings, /trash and /statistics are named by the app bar.
responsibility: Provide consistent header styling across settings/detail pages
No back arrow (#470): a page is left through the app bar (Heute, Statistik) or ⋯ -> Einstellungen

Not sticky (#615): it scrolls away with the page and the app bar alone stays, so the page gets the room. It sits in the flow below the desktop bar row; on a phone the bar is at the bottom and the header is the first thing on the page (its `pt-safe` is the only safe-area-top cover a sub-page has: it scrolls away, and `env(safe-area-inset-top)` is 0 outside a standalone install, which kan-do is not (#631); revisit with a standalone PWA)
`bg-page` surface, same as the page it sits on. A sticky element below it (.sticky-below-page-header) sticks under the app bar, not under this header
Support page-specific actions via slot
`narrow`: the title and actions sit in the same 672 px column as the content below (sub-page layout, `pageWidth: 'narrow'`, #673)

name: PropertyValueTrigger
description: The text-style trigger of a value in the task sheet's label/value rows (#72): body text whose dotted rule appears on hover and focus, the same grammar as InlineEditable. It opens a picker (the date popover) or applies a value (a timebox preset or suggestion).
usage: <PropertyValueTrigger tone="value" class="-ms-2" inset @click="open">{{ text }}</PropertyValueTrigger>; `tone` `value` (a set value), `empty` (nothing set yet), `action` (a quiet text action such as a suggestion), `picked` (the preset that is set; pass `aria-pressed`). `inset` adds the horizontal padding the sheet's rows use.
avoid: Not a button look for actions (UButton), not for the choice of one answer of a question (ChoiceChip) and not for editing text in place (InlineEditable). The trigger carries a label/value pair only inside TaskPropertyRow.
responsibility: Render one native `<button type="button">` with the `task-property-value` rule (global CSS `assets/css/task-detail.css`: dotted rule on hover and focus, faint at rest on touch screens, focus ring)
32 px tall, 44 px on a phone (`max-md:min-h-11`); text-sm; the tone sets the colour, `picked` also the weight and underline
Attributes (`aria-label`, `aria-pressed`, `data-testid`, `disabled`, handlers) land on the button

name: ResponsiveOverlay
description: The one overlay shell of the app: a centred modal (or a right-hand slideover) from 768px up, a bottom drawer below. The day close dialog and the task sheet are its hosts (#555, U12).
usage: `<ResponsiveOverlay :open="..." :title="..." @update:open="...">` with `#body` and optionally `#title`, `#description`, `#footer`. `desktop="slideover"` swaps the modal for a side sheet. The per-variant look stays with the host (`desktopUi`, `mobileUi`, `closeButton`); this component owns only the choice and the lifecycle.
avoid: The one overlay shell; a confirmation without a drawer variant may use a plain UModal.
responsibility: Picks modal/slideover vs drawer from `useIsDesktop()` and freezes the choice while the overlay is open: swapping shells would remount the hosted content and drop drafts. A resize while open takes effect after the overlay has left
Provides the frozen choice to hosted content (`useOverlayIsDesktop()`), and passes it to the `#body` and `#footer` slots as `isDesktop`

Open/close echo guard: vaul's DrawerRoot emits `update:open` with its current value on mount (page load at 390px, resize across the breakpoint). Only a value that differs from `open` is forwarded; without it a closed drawer reported `false` and a host started a close nobody asked for
`after-leave` fires for every variant

Focus into the drawer (#566): vaul cancels reka's open auto-focus (to keep the mobile keyboard closed), so the drawer never took focus and reka's trap never engaged. The drawer variant moves focus onto the drawer itself once it is mounted and again when its enter animation ends, unless hosted content already focused something inside (the task add form focuses its title field). The modal and slideover need none: reka focuses them. Hosts do not handle this
Focus handling (Escape guards, focus return) is the host's, handed in as `contentProps`

name: SectionHeader
description: Reusable section header with optional icon and configurable HTML tag
usage: Used for section titles throughout the application
avoid: Only a section title; a page title is PageHeader.
responsibility: Display section titles with consistent styling
Support optional icons
Allow semantic HTML tag selection

name: SwatchRadioGroup
description: One choice from a small set of swatches or glyphs, shown as round colour swatches or a grid of glyph cells (#72; the topic editor's Farbe and Symbol, #431). A radio group whose options are pictures, not labelled rows.
usage: <SwatchRadioGroup v-model="hue" variant="swatch" :options="[{ key: null, label: 'keine' }, { key: 'red', label: 'Rot' }]" :label="t('topic.editor.color')" item-testid="topic-hue"><template #option="{ option }">…the swatch…</template></SwatchRadioGroup>; `variant="glyph"` with `:columns="5"` for a grid (ArrowUp/Down move by a row); `@pick` fires on a click, not on arrow keys.
avoid: Not for options that carry a text label (URadioGroup), not for a card choice with an icon and a description (reka-ui RadioGroup as in LocalSetupFlow) and not for a toggle of one setting (USwitch, UCheckbox).
responsibility: Render `role="radiogroup"` with one native `<button role="radio">` per option (`aria-checked`, `aria-label` from the option); roving tabindex: the selected option (else the first) is the one Tab stop

Arrow keys move the focus and the selection to the neighbour (wrapping), Home/End to the ends, with `columns` Up/Down by a row (`utils/radioArrowKeys`); no library radio group does a grid, which is why this stays a hand-built role (decision D3 of #72)
`swatch` 28 px round (40 px on a phone, the ring marks the selection), `glyph` 40 px cells; the solid ink focus ring
Option content (the dot, the glyph) is the `option` slot; `focusSelected()` is exposed for hosts that move focus in on open
`item-testid` names the options `<prefix>-<key|none>`; attributes of the host (the group's `data-testid`) land on the group

name: InlineEditable
description: A generic component for inline editing of values.
usage: Wraps content that switches between a read-only display view and an editable input view.
avoid: Only read-or-edit in place; a form field that is always editable uses a plain input.
responsibility: Handle read/edit mode toggling
`required`: an empty value is never saved; Enter shows `requiredMessage` and stays in the editor, Esc and blur restore (kd#27)
Emit update events on save
Provide slots for custom display and input components

Keyboard-reachable edit: the read-mode trigger is `role="button"` `tabindex="0"` named "<field>: <value>"; Enter or Space edits, Enter saves, Escape cancels (and never closes the surrounding dialog), focus returns to the trigger

Hand-built `role="button"` on purpose (#72): the trigger holds block and multi-line display content (a `<button>` takes phrasing content only) and, with `interactiveDisplay`, sits beside links that must not be its descendants; a `UButton` would add a button look the row does not have

name: UpdateDialog
description: Confirmation dialog for installing a found update (#225, ADR 009). Names the new and the current version, says that data is backed up first and the app restarts, and installs only on "Installieren und neu starten". While it downloads or installs it cannot be closed.
usage: <UpdateDialog /> once in app.vue; open it with useAppUpdater().openDialog()
avoid: Only installing a found update; the after-update highlights are WhatsNewDialog.
responsibility: Footer right-aligned: neutral "Später" first, primary install button last (the one filled element)
Progress as plain text on the button ("Wird geladen… 42%"), announced in a polite live region in 10% steps
Failures stay inline and change nothing: data blocked (orange, linking to the data folder page), install failed (raspberry), with a retry
Highlights of the new version come from getUpdateNotes() (#226): with them, the line "Neu seit deiner Version (x):" labels the list (#390); without (null), "Du nutzt x." stays and no list renders

name: WhatsNewDialog
description: "What's new" after a desktop update (#226): one calm dialog with the Highlights of every version since the last one seen, newest first. Opened by the "Was ist neu" button of the post-update toast (#390) and by the re-open from the palette and /settings/updates.
usage: <WhatsNewDialog /> once in app.vue (desktop); open it with useWhatsNew()
avoid: Only after a desktop update; installing one is UpdateDialog.
responsibility: One section per version: display headline "Version X.Y.Z", then the bullets as plain body text (bold title + sentence)
Footer: single primary "Schließen" on every path; Escape, overlay and X are the same close
Text is rendered with interpolation only (never v-html); the bold title is a <strong>
No version with highlights (re-open only): one muted line

name: UButton
description: The one button of the app: solid, outline, soft, subtle, ghost and link variants in the semantic colour roles, in five sizes.
usage: Every action that is not a navigation; a text-style action inside a quiet surface is `ghost` neutral, a button that reads as a link `link`. Back and forward steps are a ghost neutral square button with `ICONS.back` / `ICONS.forward` and an `aria-label` (never a raw `<button>`). `md` is the default; the one primary action of a surface sets `size="lg"`, rows and cards use `sm`, `xs` only sits inside text (the button ladder, DESIGN.md "Buttons"). Icon-only buttons set `square` and an aria-label.
avoid: Not for navigation to a page (NuxtLink, ExternalLink for outside pages) and not for a toggle that stays pressed (UCheckbox, USwitch).

name: UDropdownMenu
description: A menu of actions or choices that opens from a button: items with a leading icon, labels, descriptions, checkbox or radio items and groups.
usage: Several secondary actions behind one trigger. The trigger is a ghost neutral `UButton`, icon-only ones set an aria-label (task sheet "more actions"); a menu that picks one of a few values shows the active one in the trigger (column sort). Action items carry a leading `i-ph-*` icon (a meaning that has an `ICONS` entry takes the glyph from there) and an i18n label; choice items (checkbox, radio) show their check instead of an icon. A destructive item sets `color: 'error'`. `:ui` only places (width, wrapping), identity lives in the theme.
avoid: Not for navigation between places (AppNav, tabs), not for right-click or long-press on a card (TaskCardContextMenu) and not for one action (a `UButton`). Not inside a drawer that has no menu primitive (NewCardFlow keeps plain buttons).

name: ULink
description: Text link to a page inside the app, with the theme's active and disabled looks.
usage: An in-app link inside a sentence (the feedback dialog's "Zugang einrichten"): `to` is a route and the caller adds the underline. Without a `class` it is unstyled apart from the theme's active colour.
avoid: Not for a page outside the app (ExternalLink: it opens the system browser on desktop), not for an action (UButton, `link` variant when it must read as text), not for a settings row (SettingsSubpageLink).

name: UBadge
description: A small label in the semantic colour roles: soft, subtle, solid and outline variants, in five sizes (the theme sets the 11 px label step for sm).
usage: A quiet status or count next to text, such as the Standard marker on a source row: `neutral` with `soft` or `subtle`, size `sm`. A domain chip with its own look (the stack pill) stays its own component.
avoid: Not a button or a link (UButton), not a notification (UAlert) and not a task-status chip (the card footer chips are custom).

name: UCard
description: A surface with optional header, body and footer; the app adds the `task` variant (the board card: elevated ground, tight padding).
usage: Only `variant="task"` for the board card (TaskCard). Grouped surfaces other than the board card use the plain hairline layout of the page, not a card.
avoid: Not a list row (ListRow) and not a modal surface (UModal); do not nest cards.

name: UChip
description: A small dot or count anchored to the corner of another element.
usage: A status dot on an icon or control (the problem dot on the app bar's more pill): `color: error`, a size from the scale, `inset` to sit on the corner. The wrapped element is the default slot.
avoid: Not a label or count in a row (UBadge) and not a notice (UAlert); it carries no text of its own, so the element it marks needs the accessible name.

name: UCollapsible
description: A trigger that shows or hides a block of content with a height animation.
usage: A secondary detail the user opens on purpose (the task sheet metadata). The default slot is the trigger, `content` the revealed part.
avoid: Not a tab set (UTabs) and not a modal; a disclosure tile with its own heading structure is StatsTile.

name: UTable
description: A data table with sortable columns, an empty text and a loading state, built on TanStack Table.
usage: Tabular records with several comparable columns (the completed-tasks table of the Statistik page, TasksTable). Pass `data` and `columns`.
avoid: Not for a list of one-line rows with actions (ListRow) and not for layout.

name: UAlert
description: The inline notice: a short message with an optional title, icon and actions in the semantic colour roles (DESIGN.md "Notices and toasts").
usage: `variant="subtle"` with `color` `error` for a failure, `warning` for "needs attention", `info` for a hint, `success` for a confirmed good result, `neutral` for a quiet result. The call site sets `role` (`alert` for a failure that appears, `status` for a state) and `data-testid`; text goes into `description` (and `title` when a second line helps). A system notice with actions is `orientation="horizontal"` (DataStorageNotice).
avoid:
Not for a field's own error (UFormField error), not for a reaction to an action that passes by (a toast, raised with `useToast`), and no hand-built tinted box or coloured `

` line next to it.

name: UForm
description: A form element that validates its fields (schema or `validate`) and focuses the first error on submit.
usage: Around a form whose fields validate together (TaskForm). Fields inside are UFormFields with a `name`; submit goes through `@submit`.
avoid: Not for one control that saves on change (InlineEditable, USwitch) and not as layout: a plain `<form>` is enough when nothing validates.

name: UFormField
description: The one field wrapper: a label, an optional description and hint, help text below the control and an error that replaces it.
usage: Around every labelled control (UInput, USelect, UTextarea, UCheckbox, USwitch): `label` names it, `help` explains it, `error` shows the failure below the control at one placement (the control gets `color="error"` and `highlight`). A visually hidden label is `:ui="{ label: 'sr-only' }"`, never a missing one.
avoid: Not around a control that has no label of its own (a title field in a card keeps its own error line), not around a button and not as a layout grid: spacing between fields belongs to the parent.

name: UCalendar
description: A month calendar to pick a date or a range, in the semantic colours and sizes.
usage: Only inside DatePickerField's popover (a single date or a range, `md`). Dates are `@internationalized/date` values, never strings.
avoid: Not a standalone page element and not for a date typed as text (UInput); a new date field is a DatePickerField.

name: UCheckbox
description: A checkbox with an optional label and description, in the semantic colours, with a list and a card variant.
usage: An independent yes/no among several, or a consent: `color="neutral"` in settings and dialogs. Always give it a `label` (or an `aria-label`).
avoid: Not for a setting that applies at once (USwitch), not for one of several exclusive options (URadioGroup) and not for a toggle button (UButton with `aria-pressed`).

name: UInput
description: The one single-line text field: outline, soft, subtle, ghost and none variants in five sizes, with leading and trailing slots, a loading state and a highlight for an error.
usage: Every typed single-line value. A labelled field sits in a UFormField (label, help, error); a field in a row of the task sheet or a card uses the `ghost` variant and its own label. Sizes in use: `sm` in rows, `md` in editors, `lg`/`xl` for a title field; keep the theme heights. An error sets `color="error"` and `highlight` and shows its text through the UFormField `error`.
avoid: Not for several lines (UTextarea), not for a choice from a list (USelect, USelectMenu) and not for editing a displayed value in place (InlineEditable).

name: URadioGroup
description: A group of exclusive options with labels and descriptions, as a list, a card or a table, vertical or horizontal.
usage: Two to five exclusive, labelled options that are all worth seeing at once: `color="neutral"`, the `list` variant. Give the group a `legend` or `aria-label`.
avoid: Not for options that are pictures (SwatchRadioGroup), not for a long list (USelect, USelectMenu) and not for independent yes/no choices (UCheckbox, USwitch).

name: USelect
description: A native-style select: pick one value from a short fixed list, shown as a field with a caret.
usage: A short, fixed list without search where a field reads better than a menu: the Notion mapping steps (always `size="lg"` inside a UFormField). Set `items` as `{ label, value }`, a `placeholder` and `aria-label` when it has no UFormField label.
avoid: Not for a list that needs search or free values (USelectMenu), not for a property value in the task sheet (TaskPropertySelect) and not for two or three options that fit as a radio group (URadioGroup).

name: USelectMenu
description: A select with a popover list, search and optional multiple values; the app theme adds the `property` variant, a plain-text trigger with a dotted rule on hover.
usage: A value from a list that needs search or free entry: the Notion priority mapping, and (as the `property` variant, wrapped by TaskPropertySelect) the property rows of the task sheet. Never set the `property` look through `:ui`.
avoid: Not for a short fixed list without search (USelect) and not for choosing one of two or three (URadioGroup); in the task sheet use TaskPropertySelect, not a bare USelectMenu.

name: USwitch
description: An on/off switch with an optional label and description; the app theme gives the off state a border and a muted thumb so it reads as off.
usage: A setting that takes effect at once (stack cards, a recap preference). `color="neutral"`, the default size; label it with `label` or `aria-label`.
avoid: Not for a choice confirmed by a save button (UCheckbox) and not for exclusive options (URadioGroup).

name: UTextarea
description: The multi-line text field: the same variants, colours and sizes as UInput, with an optional auto-resize.
usage: Several lines of free text: notes, feedback. Inside a UFormField when it has a label; `rows` sets the start height, `autoresize` grows it. Keep the default `md` size.
avoid: Not for a single line (UInput) and not for read-or-edit in place (InlineEditable with `multiline`).

name: UCommandPalette
description: A searchable list of grouped commands with a search field, keyboard navigation and an empty and a loading state.
usage: The body of the Cmd/Ctrl+K palette: `groups` of items with an icon, a label and `kbds`, `loading` while the tasks load, an `#empty` slot with EmptyNote, `:back="false"`. `:ui` only places (padding, height).
avoid: Not for navigation by pointer (AppNav, MorePanel) and not a select (USelectMenu); the palette is desktop and keyboard only.

name: UKbd
description: A keycap for a keyboard shortcut: `value` names a key (`meta`, `enter`, `arrowup`) and renders its symbol; outline, solid and subtle variants in three sizes.
usage: Shortcut hints beside a command (`kbds` of the command palette, the more panel), the default variant and size. `value` takes the key name so the platform symbol follows (⌘ on macOS, Ctrl elsewhere). The hint of an action inside a flow (NewCardFlow) is a plain `kbd` that shows on fine pointers only.
avoid: Not for a shortcut that has no visible action, not on a phone (there is no keyboard) and not as a button.

name: UTabs
description: A row of tabs that switches between views of one place; the active tab is marked by an indicator. In the theme: neutral, pill and link variants, in sm to xl.
usage: Switching between a few views of the same page (settings groups, the statistics tiles, the phone recap decks), always `:content="false"` with the page rendering the view. `pill` is the white chip on a grey track; a switcher that must reach 44 px at 390 sets `touch-target` through `:ui` (placement only). Keyboard: arrow keys move, Home/End jump.
avoid: Not for moving between places of the app (AppNav, whose selected rules are DESIGN.md "App bar"), not a step indicator (SetupRail), not a page indicator (BoardPageDots) and not a toggle for one setting (USwitch).

name: UContextMenu
description: A menu of actions that opens at the pointer on right-click or long-press.
usage: Wrapping a row or card that has quick actions (the task card); items carry icons from lib/icons.ts and a destructive item uses the error colour.
avoid: Not the only way to reach an action (it is invisible until used: every action also has a visible control) and not a dropdown from a button.

name: UDrawer
description: A panel that slides up from the bottom edge (a bottom sheet) on a phone.
usage: Only through ResponsiveOverlay (below 768 px its bottom sheet); TopicEditorHost uses it on a phone and is an inline panel from 768 px. The theme sets scrim and z-index.
avoid: Not a desktop dialog (UModal) and not a persistent side panel.

name: UModal
description: A centred dialog on a scrim: a title, a body, a footer with the actions, closed with Esc, the scrim or the close button.
usage: A confirmation or a short form on desktop. Declare the width through MODAL_WIDTH (sm confirmations, md forms, lg wide content) in the :ui prop; the footer is right-aligned by the theme. A dialog that must be a drawer on a phone is ResponsiveOverlay.
avoid: Not for a hint on hover (UTooltip), a small menu next to a control (UPopover) or an inline notice (UAlert); no ad-hoc max-width classes and no identity classes in :ui (they belong in the theme).

name: UPopover
description: A small floating panel anchored to a trigger, closed by Esc or an outside click.
usage: Pickers and short forms next to a control (date picker, topic picker, sync status); position with the content prop, size with :ui content. z-index comes from the theme.
avoid: Not a modal task (UModal), not a hint (UTooltip) and not a menu of commands (UDropdownMenu).

name: USlideover
description: A panel that slides in from the right edge.
usage: Only inside ResponsiveOverlay (the task sheet on desktop), width SHEET_WIDTH; it has a transparent overlay so the board stays visible.
avoid: Not a general dialog (UModal) and not used directly in feature code.

name: UTooltip
description: A one-line label that appears on hover or focus of its trigger.
usage: Names an icon-only control or adds a shortcut hint (kbds); the trigger keeps its own aria-label.
avoid: Not for information the user needs to proceed (put it on the page), not on touch-only controls and not for long text.
